title.zh: 卷三百二十 列傳第七十九 蔡襄 呂溱 王素 余靖 彭思永 張存
title.en: Volume 320 Biographies 79: Cai Xiang, Lu Zhen, Wang Su, Yu Jing, Peng Siyong, Zhang Cun
title.raw: 卷三百二十 列傳第七十九 蔡襄 呂溱 王素 余靖 彭思永 張存 Volume 320 Biographies 79: Cai Xiang, Lu Zhen, Wang Su, Yu Jing, Peng Siyong, Zhang Cun

sentences.zh: 蔡襄，字君謨，興化仙遊人。

translations.literal: Cai Xiang, styled Junmo, was a native of Xianyou in Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang, courtesy name Junmo, came from Xianyou in Xinghua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為西京留守推官、館閣校勘。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as a judicial aide to the military commissioner of the Western Capital and as a collator in the Imperial Archives.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as judicial aide to the Western Capital military commissioner and as a collator in the Hall of Imperial Archives.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹以言事去國，余靖論救之，尹洙請與同貶，歐陽修移書責司諫高若訥，由是三人者皆坐譴。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan was dismissed from office for speaking out on state affairs; Yu Jing memorialized in his defense; Yin Zhu requested to be demoted along with him; Ouyang Xiu sent a letter reproaching Supervisory Censor Gao Ruonuo—therefore all three were punished by demotion.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan was dismissed from court for his memorials, Yu Jing pleaded on his behalf, Yin Zhu asked to be demoted alongside him, and Ouyang Xiu wrote a letter condemning Supervisory Censor Gao Ruonuo. All three were consequently punished with demotion.

sentences.zh: 襄作《四賢一不肖詩》，都人士爭相傳寫，鬻書者市之，得厚利。

translations.literal: Xiang composed the "Poem on Four Worthies and One Unworthy"; people in the capital competed to copy and circulate it; booksellers sold it on the market and gained great profit.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang wrote the "Poem on Four Worthies and One Unworthy," which people in the capital eagerly copied and circulated; booksellers sold copies on the market at a handsome profit.

sentences.zh: 契丹使適至，買以歸，張於幽州館。

translations.literal: A Khitan envoy happened to arrive, bought it to take home, and posted it in the Khitan lodge at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A Liao envoy happened to be visiting, bought a copy to take home, and displayed it at the lodge in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，仁宗更用輔相，親擢靖、脩及王素為諫官，襄又以詩賀，三人列薦之，帝亦命襄知諫院。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingli, Emperor Renzong changed his chief ministers and personally promoted Jing, Xiu, and Wang Su as remonstrance officials; Xiang again composed a poem in congratulation; the three jointly recommended him, and the Emperor also appointed Xiang as director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Qingli era (1043), Emperor Renzong reshuffled his senior ministers and personally elevated Yu Jing, Ouyang Xiu, and Wang Su to remonstrance posts. Cai Xiang once again wrote a congratulatory poem; the three recommended him in turn, and the emperor also appointed Cai Xiang director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 襄喜言路開，而慮正人難久立也。

translations.literal: Xiang rejoiced that the avenue of speech was opened, yet worried that upright men would be hard put to remain long in office.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang was glad that the path for candid counsel had opened, but he feared that upright men would find it hard to hold their positions for long.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏曰：「朝廷增用諫臣，脩、靖、素一日並命，朝野相慶。

translations.literal: He therefore submitted a memorial saying: "The court has increased its use of remonstrance officials; Xiu, Jing, and Su were all appointed on the same day, and court and commonwealth alike rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial: "The court has newly empowered remonstrance officials—Xiu, Jing, and Su were appointed on the same day, to the rejoicing of both court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 然任諫非難，聽諫為難；

translations.literal: Yet appointing remonstrators is not the hard part—heeding remonstrance is the hard part;
translations.idiomatic: But appointing remonstrators is not the difficult thing—listening to remonstrance is.

sentences.zh: 聽諫非難，用諫為難。

translations.literal: Heeding remonstrance is not the hard part—using remonstrance is the hard part.
translations.idiomatic: And heeding remonstrance is not the difficult thing—acting on it is.

sentences.zh: 三人忠誠剛正，必能盡言。

translations.literal: The three are loyal, upright, and resolute; they will surely speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: These three men are loyal and forthright; they will surely speak their minds without reserve.

sentences.zh: 臣恐邪人不利，必造為禦之之說。

translations.literal: I fear that sinister men, finding this unfavorable to them, will surely fabricate arguments to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that men of ill intent, seeing this as harmful to themselves, will surely devise arguments to ward off their counsel.

sentences.zh: 其禦之之說不過有三，臣請為陛下辨之。

translations.literal: The arguments to guard against them are no more than three; I ask to explain them to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: There are no more than three such arguments, and I ask leave to refute them for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 一曰好名——夫忠臣引君當道，論事唯恐不至，若避好名之嫌無所陳，則土木之人，皆可為矣。

translations.literal: The first is "loving fame"—loyal ministers lead the ruler onto the proper path and fear only that their arguments on affairs will not reach full expression; if, to avoid the suspicion of loving fame, they offer nothing, then men of wood and clay could serve as well.
translations.idiomatic: The first is "craving renown." Loyal ministers guide the ruler toward the right path and speak on affairs with every ounce of conviction they possess; if, to avoid appearing fame-seekers, they held their tongues, then wooden idols could serve as ministers.

sentences.zh: 二曰好進——前世諫者之難，激於忠憤，遭世昏亂，死猶不辭，何好進之有？

translations.literal: The second is "loving advancement"—the hardships of remonstrators in former ages were stirred by loyal indignation; encountering ages of confusion and darkness, they did not refuse even death—what love of advancement was there?
translations.idiomatic: The second is "craving promotion." Remonstrators of old suffered hardship stirred by loyal outrage; in dark and chaotic times they did not shrink from death—where was any craving for advancement in that?

sentences.zh: 近世獎拔太速，但久而勿遷，雖死是官，猶無悔也。

translations.literal: In recent times rewards and promotions have come too quickly; if one simply stayed long in office without being transferred, though one died in that post, one would still have no regrets.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times promotions have come too quickly; if men were simply left in their posts without rapid transfer, they would die in those offices without regret.

sentences.zh: 三曰彰君過——諫爭之臣，蓋以司過舉耳，人主聽而行之，足以致從諫之譽，何過之能彰。

translations.literal: The third is "exposing the ruler's faults"—remonstrating ministers exist to keep watch over faults and report them; if the sovereign listens and acts, that suffices to earn the reputation of accepting remonstrance—how could faults be exposed?
translations.idiomatic: The third is "exposing the ruler's faults." Remonstrating ministers exist to detect and report errors; when the sovereign listens and acts, he earns a reputation for accepting counsel—how does that expose his faults?

sentences.zh: 至於巧者亦然，事難言則喑而不言，擇其無所忤者，時一發焉，猶或不行，則退而曰吾嘗論某事矣，此之謂好名。

translations.literal: As for the artful, it is the same: when affairs are hard to speak of they keep silent; they select what gives no offense and occasionally offer a word; if even that is not followed, they withdraw saying, "I once spoke on such-and-such a matter"—this is what is called loving fame.
translations.idiomatic: The clever operate the same way: they stay silent when matters are difficult to raise, choose topics that give no offense and speak up now and then; if even that goes unheeded, they retire saying, "I did speak on such-and-such a matter"—that is what is called craving renown.

sentences.zh: 默默容容，無所愧恥，躡資累級，以挹顯仕，此之謂好進。

translations.literal: Silent and compliant, without shame, treading rank upon rank of credentials to grasp eminent office—this is what is called loving advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Silent and compliant, without a shred of shame, climbing rung by rung to seize high office—this is what is called craving promotion.

sentences.zh: 君有過失，不救之於未然，傳之天下後世，其事愈不可掩，此之謂彰君過。

translations.literal: When the ruler has faults and offenses, not correcting them before they arise and spreading them to all under heaven and to later generations—the affair becomes all the harder to conceal—this is what is called exposing the ruler's faults.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler errs and no one corrects him before the fact, and the matter spreads throughout the realm and to posterity until it can no longer be hidden—this is what is called exposing the ruler's faults.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察之，毋使有好諫之名而無其實。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will examine this and not let there be the name of accepting good remonstrance without the reality.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to discern this clearly and not allow the court to bear the name of accepting good remonstrance without the substance.

sentences.zh: 時有旱蝗、日食、地震之變，襄以為：「災害之來，皆由人事。

translations.literal: At the time there were calamities of drought, locusts, eclipses, and earthquakes; Xiang held that "the coming of disasters all stems from human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time drought, locusts, eclipses, and earthquakes occurred in succession. Cai Xiang argued: "Disasters come entirely from human conduct.

sentences.zh: 數年以來，天戒屢至，原其所以致之，由君臣上下皆闕失也。

translations.literal: In the several years past, Heaven's warnings have repeatedly arrived; tracing the reasons that brought them about, they stem from deficiencies and failures among rulers and ministers above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warnings have come again and again in recent years; the root cause is failure and neglect at every level of the court.

sentences.zh: 不顓聽斷，不攬威權，使號令不信於人，恩澤不及於下，此陛下之失也。

translations.literal: Not concentrating on hearing and deciding, not gathering authority in one's own hands, causing commands not to be trusted among the people and grace not to reach those below—this is Your Majesty's failure.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not concentrate on hearing cases and deciding them, nor does he hold authority firmly in his own hands, so that commands are not trusted and bounty fails to reach the people below—this is Your Majesty's failing.

sentences.zh: 持天下之柄，司生民之命，無嘉謀異畫以矯時弊，不盡忠竭節以副任使，此大臣之失也。

translations.literal: Holding the handle of all under heaven and overseeing the lives of the people, yet offering no excellent plans or extraordinary measures to correct the ills of the age, not exhausting loyalty and devotion to fulfill one's commission—this is the grand ministers' failure.
translations.idiomatic: The grand ministers hold the reins of empire and hold the lives of the people in their charge, yet offer no worthy plans to remedy the ills of the age and do not exhaust their loyalty to fulfill their duties—this is their failing.

sentences.zh: 朝有敝政而不能正，民有疾苦而不能去，陛下寬仁少斷而不能規，大臣循默避事而不能斥，此臣等之罪也。

translations.literal: The court has corrupt policies that cannot be corrected, the people have hardships and pain that cannot be removed, Your Majesty is lenient and benevolent but seldom decisive and cannot be remonstrated with, grand ministers follow routine and keep silent to avoid affairs and cannot be dismissed—this is our guilt as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt policies go uncorrected at court, the people's suffering goes unrelieved, Your Majesty's lenience and reluctance to decide goes unremonstrated with, and grand ministers' silence and evasion goes unpunished—this is the guilt of us, your ministers.

sentences.zh: 陛下既有引過之言，達於天地神祇矣，願思其實以應之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already voiced words of taking blame, reaching Heaven and Earth and the spirits; I hope you will consider the substance to respond accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already spoken words of self-reproach that have reached Heaven, Earth, and the spirits; I hope you will match those words with real action.

sentences.zh: 疏出，聞者皆悚然。

translations.literal: When the memorial was issued, all who heard it were struck with awe.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was circulated, all who read it were deeply shaken.

sentences.zh: 進直史館，兼修起居注，襄益任職論事，無所回撓。

translations.literal: He was promoted to appointment in the Direct Historiography Office and concurrently compiled the Daily Record; Xiang all the more discharged his duties in memorializing on affairs, without any wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to duty in the Historiography Office and appointed concurrently to compile the Daily Record, Cai Xiang grew all the more resolute in memorializing on affairs, never yielding.

sentences.zh: 開寶浮圖災，下有舊瘞佛舍利，詔取以入，宮人多灼臂落髮者。

translations.literal: The Kaibao pagoda suffered a fire; beneath it were old buried Buddhist relics; an edict ordered them taken into the palace, and many palace women burned their arms and cut their hair.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kaibao Pagoda burned, old buried Buddhist relics were found beneath it. An edict ordered them brought into the palace, and many palace women burned their arms and shaved their heads in devotion.

sentences.zh: 方議復營之，襄諫曰：「非理之福，不可徼幸。

translations.literal: Just as rebuilding was under discussion, Xiang remonstrated saying: "Blessings that are contrary to reason cannot be sought by luck.
translations.idiomatic: As a plan to rebuild the pagoda was being discussed, Cai Xiang remonstrated: "Blessing that runs against reason cannot be courted through luck.

sentences.zh: 今生民困苦，四夷驕慢，陛下當修人事，奈何專信佛法？

translations.literal: Now the people are in hardship and distress, the four barbarians are arrogant and insolent—Your Majesty ought to cultivate human affairs; why rely exclusively on Buddhist teaching?
translations.idiomatic: The people are suffering, the foreign tribes grow arrogant—Your Majesty should set human affairs in order; why rely solely on Buddhism?

sentences.zh: 或以舍利有光，推為神異，彼其所居尚不能護，何有於威靈。

translations.literal: Some take the relics' radiance as proof of divine wonder; yet they could not even protect the place where they resided—what talk is there of numinous power?
translations.idiomatic: Some point to the relics' glow as proof of the miraculous, yet they could not even protect their own dwelling—what numinous power is there in them?

sentences.zh: 天之降災，以示儆戒，顧大興功役，是將以人力排天意也。」

translations.literal: Heaven sends down calamities to serve as warnings and admonitions; yet to undertake great construction projects on the contrary is to use human effort to oppose Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sends calamities as warnings; to launch grand construction projects in response is to use human labor to defy Heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 呂夷簡平章國事，宰相以下就其第議政事，襄奏請罷之。

translations.literal: Lü Yijian was concurrent Director of State Affairs; chancellors and those below went to his residence to discuss state affairs; Xiang memorialized requesting that this be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With Lü Yijian serving as concurrent Director of State Affairs, chancellors and subordinates went to his home to discuss state business. Cai Xiang memorialized asking that this practice be ended.

sentences.zh: 元昊納款，始自稱「兀卒」，既又譯為「吾祖」。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao submitted allegiance; at first he called himself "Wuzu," which was then translated as "My Forefather."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao submitted to the Song, he first styled himself "Wuzu," which was then rendered in Chinese as "My Forefather."

sentences.zh: 襄言：「『吾祖』猶云『我翁』，慢侮甚矣。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "'My Forefather' is like saying 'my old man'—the contempt and insult is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang said: "'My Forefather' amounts to saying 'my old man'—the insult is profound.

sentences.zh: 使朝廷賜之詔，而亦曰『吾祖』，是何等語邪？」

translations.literal: If the court were to bestow an edict upon him and also say 'My Forefather,' what manner of language would that be?
translations.idiomatic: If the court issued an edict addressing him as 'My Forefather,' what sort of language would that be?"

sentences.zh: 夏竦罷樞密使，韓琦、范仲淹在位，襄言：「陛下罷竦而用琦、仲淹，士大夫賀於朝，庶民歌於路，至飲酒叫號以為歡。

translations.literal: Xia Song was removed as Military Affairs Commissioner; Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan held office; Xiang said: "Your Majesty removed Song and employed Qi and Zhongyan; scholar-officials congratulated at court, common people sang on the roads, even drinking wine and shouting in celebration.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Song was removed as Military Affairs Commissioner and Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan took office, Cai Xiang said: "Your Majesty dismissed Song and appointed Qi and Zhongyan; officials celebrated at court and common folk sang in the streets, some drinking and shouting for joy.

sentences.zh: 且退一邪，進一賢，豈遂能關天下輕重哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, removing one evil man and advancing one worthy—is that really enough to turn the weight of all under heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Removing one corrupt man and advancing one worthy—can that alone shift the fortunes of the realm?

sentences.zh: 蓋一邪退則其類退，一賢進則其類進。

translations.literal: For when one evil man retreats, his kind retreats; when one worthy advances, his kind advances.
translations.idiomatic: When one corrupt man is dismissed, his like are dismissed; when one worthy man is promoted, his like are promoted.

sentences.zh: 眾邪並退，眾賢並進，海內有不泰乎！

translations.literal: When all evil men retreat together and all worthies advance together, is there anywhere within the seas that would not be at peace!
translations.idiomatic: When the corrupt are cleared out together and the worthy rise together, how could the realm not prosper!

sentences.zh: 雖然，臣切憂之。

translations.literal: Even so, I am deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, I am deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 天下之勢，譬猶病者，陛下既得良醫矣，信任不疑，非徒愈病，而又壽民。

translations.literal: The condition of all under heaven is like a sick man; Your Majesty has already obtained good physicians; if you trust them without doubt, you will not merely cure the illness but also extend the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: The state of the realm is like a sick patient; Your Majesty has found capable physicians—if you trust them fully, you will not merely cure the illness but prolong the life of the people.

sentences.zh: 醫雖良術。

translations.literal: Though the physicians are skilled in their art.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled though the physicians may be,

sentences.zh: 不得盡用，則病且日深，雖有和、扁，難責效矣。」

translations.literal: If their methods cannot be fully employed, then the illness will daily deepen; even though you had He Qubo and Bian Que, you could not demand results.
translations.idiomatic: if their remedies cannot be fully applied, the illness will only deepen day by day; even He Qubo and Bian Que could not be expected to cure it."

sentences.zh: 保州卒作亂，推懦兵十餘輩為首惡，殺之以求招撫。

translations.literal: Soldiers at Baozhou mutinied; more than ten timid soldiers were put forward as ringleaders and killed in order to seek pacification through inducement.
translations.idiomatic: Troops at Baozhou mutinied; more than a dozen low-ranking soldiers were singled out as ringleaders and executed in a bid to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「天下兵百萬，苟無誅殺決行之令，必開驕慢暴亂之源。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "Soldiers throughout the realm number a million; if there is no order for resolute execution and punishment, this will surely open the source of arrogance, insolence, and violent rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang said: "There are a million troops in the empire; without firm orders for execution and punishment, this will open the door to arrogance and mutiny.

sentences.zh: 今州兵戕官吏、閉城門，不能討，從而招之，豈不為四方笑。

translations.literal: Now state soldiers kill officials and shut the city gates, yet we cannot punish them and instead follow with pacification—would this not make us laughed at throughout the four directions?
translations.idiomatic: When garrison troops kill officials and shut the city gates, and we cannot suppress them but instead offer pacification, will we not become a laughingstock everywhere?

sentences.zh: 乞將兵入城，盡誅之。」

translations.literal: I beg to lead troops into the city and execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that troops be sent into the city to execute them all.

sentences.zh: 詔從其議。

translations.literal: An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 以母老，求知福州，改福建路轉運使，開古五塘溉民田，奏減五代時丁口稅之半。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he requested appointment as prefect of Fuzhou and was changed to Transport Commissioner of the Fujian Circuit; he opened the ancient Five Ponds to irrigate the people's fields and memorialized to reduce the per-capita tax of the Five Dynasties period by half.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly, he asked to be prefect of Fuzhou and was instead made transport commissioner for Fujian Circuit. He reopened the ancient Five Ponds to irrigate farmland and memorialized to cut the Five Dynasties per-capita tax in half.

sentences.zh: 復修起居注。

translations.literal: He again compiled the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as compiler of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 唐介擊宰相，觸盛怒，襄趨進曰：「介誠狂愚，然出於進忠，必望全貸。」

translations.literal: Tang Jie struck the chancellor, provoking great anger; Xiang hurried forward and said: "Jie is indeed rash and foolish, yet he acted from loyalty; I must hope for complete pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Jie struck the chancellor, provoking the emperor's fury, Cai Xiang stepped forward and said: "Jie was indeed reckless and foolish, but he acted out of loyalty; I beg that he be fully spared.

sentences.zh: 既貶春州，又上疏以為此必死之謫，得改英州。

translations.literal: After he was demoted to Chunzhou, Xiang again submitted a memorial arguing that this was a posting where death was certain, and the sentence was changed to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang Jie was demoted to Chunzhou, Cai Xiang submitted another memorial arguing that this was a posting tantamount to a death sentence, and the demotion was changed to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 溫成后追冊，請勿立忌，而罷監護園陵官。

translations.literal: When Empress Wencheng was posthumously ennobled, he requested that no anniversary observance be established and that the officials overseeing the imperial tombs be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wencheng was posthumously ennobled, he asked that no anniversary memorial be established and that tomb-guard officials be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 進知制誥，三御史論梁適解職，襄不草制。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Edicts; the three censorial officials memorialized on Liang Shi's removal from office, and Xiang refused to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to draftsman of edicts, when three censorial officials argued for Liang Shi's dismissal, Cai Xiang refused to draft the dismissal edict.

sentences.zh: 後每除授非當職，輒封還之。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever appointments were not appropriate to the office, he would seal and return them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever he judged an appointment improper for the office, he sealed and returned the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝遇之益厚，賜其母冠帔以示寵，又親書「君謨」兩字，遣使持詔予之。

translations.literal: The Emperor treated him with ever greater favor, bestowed upon his mother a cap and sash to show esteem, and personally wrote the two characters "Junmo," sending an envoy with an edict to grant them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him with growing favor, granted his mother ceremonial dress as a mark of grace, and personally wrote the two characters "Junmo," sending an envoy to bestow them by edict.

sentences.zh: 遷龍圖閣直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Academician Directly Attached to the Hall of Dragon Designs and made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Dragon Designs Pavilion and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 襄精吏事，談笑剖決，破奸發隱，吏不能欺。

translations.literal: Xiang was skilled in administrative matters; he decided cases amid conversation and laughter, exposed treachery and uncovered hidden wrongs, and clerks could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang was masterful in administrative affairs, deciding cases with ease while unmasking fraud and uncovering hidden crimes; his clerks could not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 以樞密直學士再知福州。

translations.literal: As Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs he again served as prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, he served again as prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡士周希孟、陳烈、陳襄、鄭穆以行義著，襄備禮招延，誨諸生以經學。

translations.literal: Local scholars Zhou Ximeng, Chen Lie, Chen Xiang, and Zheng Mu were renowned for conduct and righteousness; Xiang treated them with full ceremony in inviting them and instructed students in classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Local scholars Zhou Ximeng, Chen Lie, Chen Xiang, and Zheng Mu were known for their integrity; Cai Xiang invited them with full courtesy and instructed students in the classics.

sentences.zh: 俗重凶儀，親亡或秘不舉，至破產飯僧，下令禁止之。

translations.literal: Custom attached great weight to funeral rites; when parents died some kept it secret and did not announce it, even to the point of ruining families to feed monks; he issued an order forbidding this.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom placed excessive emphasis on funeral rites; some families hid deaths and failed to report them, ruining themselves to feast monks. He issued an order forbidding the practice.

sentences.zh: 徙知泉州，距州二十里萬安渡，絕海而濟，往來畏其險。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Quanzhou; twenty li from the prefectural seat was Wan'an Ford, where one crossed over open sea, and travelers feared its danger.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Quanzhou prefect, he faced the Wan'an Crossing twenty li from the city, where travelers crossed open sea and feared the peril.

sentences.zh: 襄立石為梁，其長三百六十丈，種蠣於礎以為固，至今賴焉。

translations.literal: Xiang erected a stone bridge; it was three hundred and sixty zhang in length; he planted oysters on the foundations to strengthen it, and to this day people rely upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang built a stone bridge three hundred and sixty zhang long, planting oysters on the foundations to bind them—a bridge people rely on to this day.

sentences.zh: 又植松七百里以庇道路，閩人刻碑紀德。

translations.literal: He also planted pines for seven hundred li to shelter the roads, and people of Min carved steles to record his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He also planted pines along seven hundred li of road to provide shade, and the people of Fujian erected steles in his honor.

sentences.zh: 召為翰林學士、三司使，較天下盈虛出入，量力以制用。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician and Commissioner of the Three Departments; he compared revenues and expenditures throughout the realm and regulated use according to capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as Hanlin academician and commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments, he assessed national revenues and expenditures and regulated spending according to capacity.

sentences.zh: 剗剔蠹敝，簿書紀綱纖悉皆可法。

translations.literal: He cut away corruption and abuses; ledgers and records, major and minor, all could serve as models.
translations.idiomatic: He rooted out corruption and waste; his account books and administrative standards, down to the smallest detail, became models for all.

sentences.zh: 英宗不豫，皇太后聽政，為輔臣言：「先帝既立皇子，宦妾更加熒惑，而近臣知名者亦然，幾敗大事，近已焚其章矣。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong fell ill, the Empress Dowager held court; she told the chief ministers: "The late Emperor had already established the crown prince, yet palace concubines further beguiled him, and famous members of the inner circle did likewise, nearly ruining a great affair; their petitions have recently been burned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong fell ill and the empress dowager regent addressed the chief ministers, she said: "The late emperor had already named the heir, but palace women and well-known inner-circle officials tried to sway him further, nearly wrecking the succession; their memorials have now been burned.

sentences.zh: 已而外人遂云襄有論議，帝聞而疑之。

translations.literal: Before long outsiders said that Xiang had offered opinions on this, and when the Emperor heard of it he grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Word then spread outside the palace that Cai Xiang had spoken on the matter, and the emperor grew suspicious when he heard it.

sentences.zh: 會襄數謁告，因命擇人代襄。

translations.literal: As it happened Xiang repeatedly requested leave, and therefore an order was issued to choose someone to replace Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: As Cai Xiang repeatedly requested leave, the emperor ordered a replacement to be chosen.

sentences.zh: 襄乞為杭州，拜端明殿學士以往。

translations.literal: Xiang requested to be sent to Hangzhou and was appointed Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity to proceed there.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang asked to be sent to Hangzhou and was appointed academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity for that posting.

sentences.zh: 治平三年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiping he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhiping era (1066), he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 襄工於書，為當時第一，仁宗尤愛之，製《元舅隴西王碑文》命書之。

translations.literal: Xiang was skilled in calligraphy and ranked first in his time; Emperor Renzong especially cherished him and composed the "Epitaph for the Prince of Longxi, Imperial Maternal Uncle" ordering him to inscribe it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang was a master calligrapher, considered the finest of his age. Emperor Renzong especially favored him and had him inscribe the epitaph for the Prince of Longxi, his maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 及令書《溫成后父碑》，則曰：「此待詔職耳。」

translations.literal: When ordered to inscribe the "Stele for the Empress Wencheng's Father," he said: "This is merely the work of a court calligrapher.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to inscribe the stele for Empress Wencheng's father, he said, "That is merely the work of a court calligrapher.

sentences.zh: 不奉詔。

translations.literal: He did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the order.

sentences.zh: 於朋友尚信義，聞其喪，則不御酒肉，為位而哭。

translations.literal: Toward friends he valued faith and righteousness; when he heard of their bereavement, he would abstain from wine and meat and set up a seat to weep.
translations.idiomatic: He held faith and loyalty sacred among friends; on news of a friend's death he abstained from wine and meat and wept at a mourning seat.

sentences.zh: 嘗飲會靈東園，坐客誤射矢傷人，遽指襄。

translations.literal: Once while drinking at the Eastern Garden of the Hall of Assembled Spirits, a seated guest accidentally shot an arrow and wounded someone, and immediately pointed at Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once while dining at the Eastern Garden of the Hall of Assembled Spirits, a guest accidentally shot someone with an arrow and immediately blamed Cai Xiang.

sentences.zh: 他日帝問之，再拜愧謝，終不自辨。

translations.literal: Another day when the Emperor asked about it, he bowed twice in ashamed apology and never defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor later asked him about it, he bowed in apology and never offered a word in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 蔡京與同郡而晚出，欲附名閥，自謂為族弟。

translations.literal: Cai Jing was from the same commandery but came later; wishing to attach himself to a distinguished clan, he called himself a clansman younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing was from the same region but of a later generation; seeking to attach himself to a prominent clan, he claimed to be Cai Xiang's clansman and junior.

sentences.zh: 政和初，襄孫佃廷試唱名，居舉首，京侍殿上，以族孫引嫌，降為第二，佃終身恨之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenghe era, Xiang's grandson Dian topped the palace examination roll call; Jing attended at the palace hall and, citing relationship as clansman and grandson, recused himself and lowered Dian to second place; Dian resented this all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenghe era, Cai Xiang's grandson Dian ranked first when palace examination names were announced. Cai Jing, attending at court, cited kinship as grounds for recusal and demoted him to second place—a slight Dian resented for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，賜襄諡曰忠惠。

translations.literal: In the Qiandao era, Xiang was granted the posthumous title Zhonghui (Loyal and Kind).
translations.idiomatic: In the Qiandao era (1165–1173), Cai Xiang was granted the posthumous epithet Loyal and Beneficent.

sentences.zh: 呂溱，字濟叔，揚州人。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen, styled Jishu, was a native of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen, courtesy name Jishu, was a native of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 進士第一。

translations.literal: He ranked first among jinshi graduates.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first on the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 通判亳州，直集賢院，同修起居注。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Bozhou, was appointed directly to the Academy of Assembled Worthies, and jointly compiled the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Bozhou, was appointed to the Academy of Worthies, and helped compile the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 坐預進奏院宴飲，出知蘄、楚、舒三州。

translations.literal: He was punished for participating in a banquet at the Imperial Bulletin Office and was sent out to serve as prefect of Qi, Chu, and Shu prefectures in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for attending a feast at the Imperial Bulletin Office, he was posted in succession as prefect of Qi, Chu, and Shu.

sentences.zh: 復修起居注。

translations.literal: He again compiled the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as compiler of the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 儂智高寇嶺南，詔奏邸毋得輒報。

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao raided Lingnan; an edict ordered that the memorial office must not report this on its own authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao invaded Lingnan, an edict forbade the memorial transmission office from reporting the news on its own.

sentences.zh: 溱言：「一方有警，使諸道聞之，共得為備。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "When one region has an alarm, letting all circuits hear of it allows them jointly to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen said: "When one region faces an emergency, every circuit should hear of it so all can prepare together.

sentences.zh: 今欲人不知，此何意也。」

translations.literal: Now you wish people not to know—what meaning is in this?
translations.idiomatic: To want no one to know—what is the purpose of that?

sentences.zh: 進知制誥，又出知杭州，入為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Edicts; he was again sent out as prefect of Hangzhou, then entered court as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to draftsman of edicts, he was then posted as prefect of Hangzhou before returning to court as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 疏論宰相陳執中奸邪，仁宗還其疏。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing Chancellor Chen Zhizhong's wickedness and treachery; Emperor Renzong returned his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized accusing Chancellor Chen Zhizhong of treachery; Emperor Renzong returned the memorial unread.

sentences.zh: 溱曰：「以口舌論人，是陰中大臣也。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "To judge a man with words of the mouth and tongue is to strike at a grand minister in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen said: "To judge a man by mere words is to attack a grand minister in secret.

sentences.zh: 願出以示執中，使得自辨。」

translations.literal: I wish it to be released and shown to Zhizhong so that he may defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that it be shown to Zhizhong so he may answer for himself.

sentences.zh: 未幾，執中去，溱亦以侍讀學士知徐州，賜宴資善堂，遣使諭曰：「此特為卿設，宜盡醉也。」

translations.literal: Before long Zhizhong was removed; Zhen also served as Prefect of Xuzhou as Academician Reader-in-Waiting; a feast was granted at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness, and an envoy was sent with the message: "This feast is set specially for you; you should drink your fill.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chen Zhizhong was dismissed. Lü Zhen was posted as prefect of Xuzhou while serving as reader-in-waiting. The emperor granted him a feast at the Hall of Cultivating Goodness and sent word: "This feast is held especially for you; drink your fill.

sentences.zh: 詔自今由經筵出者視為例。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from this time forth those departing from the classics lecture hall should be treated as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that henceforth officials leaving the classics lecture hall would receive the same honor as precedent.

sentences.zh: 徙成德軍，時方開六塔河，宰相主其議。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chengdé Army; at the time the Six Pagodas Canal was being opened, and the chancellor championed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Chengdé Army, he arrived as work on the Six Pagoda Canal was underway, a project the chancellor strongly supported.

sentences.zh: 會地震，溱請罷之，以答天戒。

translations.literal: When an earthquake occurred, Zhen requested that it be halted to respond to Heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: When an earthquake struck, Lü Zhen asked that the project be stopped as a response to Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 溱豪侈自放，簡忽於事。

translations.literal: Zhen was extravagant and self-indulgent, negligent in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen lived extravagantly and was careless in his duties.

sentences.zh: 與都轉運使李參不相能，還，判流內銓，參劾其借官麹作酒，以私貨往河東貿易，及違式受饋贐，事下大理議。

translations.literal: He did not get along with Metropolitan Transport Commissioner Li Can; returning to court, he was assigned to the Internal Personnel Selection Bureau; Can impeached him for using official malt to brew wine, taking private goods to trade in Hedong, and improperly accepting farewell gifts; the case was referred to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At odds with metropolitan transport commissioner Li Can, he returned to court and was assigned to the internal personnel bureau. Li Can impeached him for using official malt to brew wine, trading private goods in Hedong, and improperly accepting farewell gifts; the case went to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 溱乃未嘗受，而外廷紛然謂溱有死罪。

translations.literal: Zhen had in fact never accepted them, yet the outer court clamored that Zhen deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen had in fact never accepted the gifts, yet officials outside the palace clamored that he deserved death.

sentences.zh: 帝知其過輕，但貶秩，知和州。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew his offenses were minor and merely reduced his rank, appointing him prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew his offenses were minor and merely reduced his rank, posting him as prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 御史以為未抵罪，分司南京。

translations.literal: Censors thought this did not match his guilt and assigned him to branch service at the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Censors thought the punishment insufficient and he was assigned to branch service at the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 起知池州、江寧府，復集賢院學士，加龍圖閣直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Chizhou and Jiangning Prefecture, restored as academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, promoted to Academician Directly Attached to the Hall of Dragon Designs, and made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as prefect of Chizhou and Jiangning, restored as an Academy of Worthies academician, promoted to academician of the Dragon Designs Pavilion, and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時為京尹者比不稱職，溱精識過人，辨訟立斷，豪惡斂跡。

translations.literal: Prefects of the capital had generally not performed well; Zhen's keen insight surpassed others, he decided lawsuits on the spot, and the powerful and wicked drew in their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects of the capital had generally failed in their duties; Lü Zhen's sharp judgment surpassed others, he decided cases on the spot, and the powerful and wicked fell silent.

sentences.zh: 嘗以職事對，神宗察其有疾色，勉以近醫藥，已而果病。

translations.literal: Once when he reported on his duties, Emperor Shenzong noticed he looked ill and urged him to seek medical treatment; before long he did fall ill.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he reported on his duties, Emperor Shenzong noticed he looked unwell and urged him to see a physician; before long he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 改樞密直學士、提舉醴泉觀，遂卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: He was changed to Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs and placed in charge of the Liquan Abbey, then died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs and placed in charge of the Liquan Abbey, he soon died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 帝悼念之，詔中書曰：「溱立朝最孤，知事君之節，絕跡權貴，故中廢十餘年，人無言者。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned him and issued an edict the Secretariat: "Zhen stood alone at court most of all, knowing the integrity of serving one's ruler, keeping far from the powerful and noble; therefore he was suspended for more than ten years, and no one spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and instructed the Secretariat: "Zhen stood alone at court, knowing how to serve his ruler with integrity and keeping his distance from the powerful; for this he was sidelined for more than ten years, and no one spoke up for him.

sentences.zh: 方擢領要劇，而奄忽淪亡，家貧子幼，遭此大禍，必至狼狽。

translations.literal: Just as he was promoted to head important and arduous posts, he suddenly perished; his family was poor and his children young; suffering this great calamity, they would surely be reduced to distress.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was promoted to demanding posts of great responsibility, he died suddenly. His family was poor and his children young; faced with this catastrophe, they would surely be left in dire straits.

sentences.zh: 宜優給賻禮，官庀其葬，以厲臣節。」

translations.literal: He should be generously granted funeral gifts, and the government should arrange his burial, to encourage the integrity of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He should receive generous funeral provisions, and the government should arrange his burial, to encourage ministerial integrity.

sentences.zh: 敕其婦兄護喪歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his wife's elder brother to escort the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his wife's elder brother to escort the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 溱開敏，善議論，一時名輩皆推許。

translations.literal: Zhen was quick-witted and clever, skilled in debate; eminent men of the time all praised and approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen was quick-witted and eloquent; leading figures of the day all praised him.

sentences.zh: 然自貴重，在杭州接賓客，不過數語，時目為「七字舍人」云。

translations.literal: Yet he held himself in high esteem; when receiving guests in Hangzhou he spoke no more than a few words, and people of the time called him the "Seven-Character Academician."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he held himself in high esteem; when receiving guests in Hangzhou he spoke only a few words, and people called him the "Seven-Character Academician."

sentences.zh: 王素，字仲儀，太尉旦季子也。

translations.literal: Wang Su, styled Zhongyi, was the youngest son of Grand Marshal Wang Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, courtesy name Zhongyi, was the youngest son of Grand Marshal Wang Dan.

sentences.zh: 賜進士出身，至屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: Granted jinshi status, he rose to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Granted jinshi status, he rose to assistant director in the Ministry of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞孔道輔薦為侍御史。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Kong Daofu recommended him as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Kong Daofu recommended him as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 道輔貶，出知鄂州。

translations.literal: When Daofu was demoted, Su was sent out as prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Daofu was demoted, Wang Su was posted as prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗思其賢，擢知諫院。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong recalled his worth and promoted him to director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong, mindful of his talent, promoted him to director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 素方壯年，遇事感發。

translations.literal: Su was still in the prime of life and was stirred to action by affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Still in the prime of life, Wang Su was stirred to action by every affair that came before him.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「今中外無名之費，倍蓰於前，請省其非急者。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Today nameless expenditures inside and outside the court have multiplied over what came before; I ask that those that are not urgent be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Unnecessary expenditures at court and throughout the realm have multiplied; I ask that nonessential spending be cut.

sentences.zh: 適皇子生，將進百僚以官，惠諸軍以賞。

translations.literal: Just then a prince was born; the court was about to advance all officials in rank and bestow rewards on the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a prince was born, and the court planned to promote all officials and reward the armies.

sentences.zh: 素爭曰：「今西夏畔渙，契丹要求，縣官之須，且日急矣。

translations.literal: Su argued: "Now the Western Xia rebels and scatters, the Khitan makes demands, and the needs of the treasury grow more urgent by the day.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su objected: "The Western Xia is in revolt, the Khitan is pressing demands, and the treasury's needs grow more urgent by the day.

sentences.zh: 宜留爵秩以賞戰功，儲金繒以佐邊費。」

translations.literal: Ranks and titles should be reserved to reward military merit, and gold and silk stored to assist border expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks and titles should be reserved to reward military merit, and gold and silk saved to fund the border.

sentences.zh: 議遂已。

translations.literal: The plan was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 京師旱，素請帝禱於郊，帝曰：「太史言月二日當雨，今將以旦日出禱。」

translations.literal: The capital suffered drought; Su asked the Emperor to pray at the suburban altar; the Emperor said: "The Grand Astrologer says it will rain on the second of the month; I will go out to pray at dawn on that day.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital suffered drought, Wang Su asked the emperor to pray at the suburban altar. The emperor said: "The grand astrologer says it will rain on the second of the month; I will go out to pray at dawn that day.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「臣非太史，然度是日必不雨。」

translations.literal: Su said: "I am no grand astrologer, yet I judge that on that day it will surely not rain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "I am no astrologer, but I am certain it will not rain that day.

sentences.zh: 帝問故，曰：「陛下知其且雨而禱之，應天不以誠，故臣知不雨。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked why; he said: "Your Majesty knows it will rain and yet goes to pray—responding to Heaven without sincerity; therefore I know it will not rain.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, he said: "Your Majesty knows rain is coming yet still goes to pray—responding to Heaven without sincerity. That is why I know it will not rain.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則明日詣醴泉觀。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Then tomorrow I will go to the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Then tomorrow I will go to the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「醴泉之近，猶外朝耳，豈憚暑不遠出邪？」

translations.literal: Su said: "The Liquan Abbey is nearby—it is still the outer court; are you afraid of the heat and unwilling to go far?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "The Liquan Abbey is nearby—it is still within the outer court. Are you unwilling to go farther because of the heat?"

sentences.zh: 帝悚然。

translations.literal: The Emperor was startled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled.

sentences.zh: 更詔詣西太一宮，諫官故不在屬車間，乃命素扈從。

translations.literal: He changed the edict to go to the Western Grand Unity Palace; remonstrance officials were customarily not among the accompanying carriages, so he ordered Su to attend as escort.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the edict to go to the Western Grand Unity Palace. Remonstrance officials were not customarily among the accompanying carriages, so he ordered Wang Su to attend as escort.

sentences.zh: 日甚熾，埃氛翳空，比輿駕還，未薄城，天大雷電而雨。

translations.literal: The sun burned fiercely and dust veiled the sky; just as the imperial carriage returned and had not yet reached the city walls, Heaven sent great thunder and lightning and rain.
translations.idiomatic: The sun blazed and dust filled the sky. Just as the imperial carriage returned and had not yet reached the city walls, thunder cracked and rain poured down.

sentences.zh: 王德用進二女子，素論之，帝曰：「朕真宗皇帝之子，卿王旦之子，有世舊，非他人比也。

translations.literal: Wang Deyong presented two women; Su remonstrated; the Emperor said: "I am the son of Emperor Zhenzong, you are the son of Wang Dan—we have ties across generations and are not to be compared with others.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Deyong presented two women to the court, Wang Su remonstrated. The emperor said: "I am the son of Emperor Zhenzong, and you are the son of Wang Dan—we have ties across generations and are not like other men.

sentences.zh: 德用實進女，然已事朕左右，奈何？」

translations.literal: Deyong did in fact present women, yet they already serve at my side—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Deyong did present women, and they already serve at my side—what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 素曰：「臣之憂正恐在左右爾。」

translations.literal: Su said: "My worry is precisely that they are at Your Majesty's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "My worry is precisely that they are at Your Majesty's side."

sentences.zh: 帝動容，立命遣二女出。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved and immediately ordered the two women sent out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and immediately ordered the two women dismissed.

sentences.zh: 賜素銀緋，擢天章閣待制、淮南都轉運按察使。

translations.literal: Su was granted silver-red robes and promoted to Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and Metropolitan Transport and Investigation Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was granted silver-red robes and promoted to awaiting draftsman of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and metropolitan transport and investigation commissioner for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 時新置按察，類多以苛為明。

translations.literal: At the time the investigation posts were newly established, and most used severity to show their clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation posts had been newly established, and most commissioners used harshness to display their acumen.

sentences.zh: 素獨不擿細故，即有貪刻，必繩治窮竟，以故下吏愛而畏之。

translations.literal: Su alone did not pick at minor matters; when there was greed or harshness, he would pursue punishment to the end; for this reason subordinate officials both loved and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su alone did not pick at minor matters; when he found greed or cruelty, he pursued punishment to the end. Subordinate officials both loved and feared him.

sentences.zh: 改知渭州，坐市木河東有擾民狀，降華州，又奪職徙汝。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Weizhou; punished for purchasing timber in Hedong in a manner that disturbed the people, he was demoted to Huazhou, then stripped of office and transferred to Ru prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Weizhou prefect, he was demoted to Huazhou for purchasing timber in Hedong in a way that harmed the people, then stripped of office and posted to Ru.

sentences.zh: 俄悉還其故，遷龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: Before long all his former honors were restored and he was promoted to Academician Directly Attached to the Hall of Dragon Designs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long all his former honors were restored and he was promoted to academician of the Dragon Designs Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 初，原州蔣偕建議築大蟲巉堡，宣撫使聽之。

translations.literal: Initially, Jiang Jie of Yuanzhou proposed building the Great Worm Cliff Fort; the pacification commissioner approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Jiang Jie of Yuanzhou proposed building Great Worm Cliff Fort, and the pacification commissioner approved it.

sentences.zh: 役未具，敵伺間要擊，不得成。

translations.literal: Before the labor was ready, the enemy watched for an opening and intercepted them, and the fort could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the work was ready, the enemy intercepted them and the fort could not be completed.

sentences.zh: 偕懼來歸死。

translations.literal: Jie, in fear, returned to court to accept death.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, in fear, returned to court expecting execution.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「若罪偕，乃是墮敵計。」

translations.literal: Su said: "If Jie is punished, that would simply fall into the enemy's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "If Jie is punished, we will simply have fallen into the enemy's trap."

sentences.zh: 責偕使畢力自效。

translations.literal: He charged Jie to exert his full strength in loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Jiang Jie to exert his full strength in loyal service.

sentences.zh: 總管狄青曰：「偕往益敗，不可遣。」

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Di Qing said: "If Jie goes, defeat will only increase; he must not be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Di Qing said: "If Jie goes, defeat will only worsen; he must not be sent."

sentences.zh: 素曰：「偕敗則總管行，總管敗，素即行矣。」

translations.literal: Su said: "If Jie is defeated, then the commander-in-chief will go; if the commander-in-chief is defeated, then Su will go.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "If Jie is defeated, the commander-in-chief will go; if the commander-in-chief is defeated, I will go myself."

sentences.zh: 青不敢復言，偕卒城而還。

translations.literal: Qing dared speak no further; Jie ultimately completed the fort and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing said no more; Jiang Jie completed the fort and returned.

sentences.zh: 以樞密直學士知開封府。

translations.literal: As Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs he served as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: As academician directly attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, he served as prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 至和秋，大雨，蔡河裂，水入城。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the Zhihe era, heavy rains burst the Cai River and water entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the Zhihe era, heavy rains burst the Cai River and floodwater entered the city.

sentences.zh: 詔軍吏障朱雀門，素曰：「皇上不豫，兵民廬舍多覆壓，眾心怦怦然，奈何更塞門以動眾。」

translations.literal: An edict ordered military officers to block the Vermilion Bird Gate; Su said: "The Emperor is unwell, many military and civilian dwellings have been crushed, the people's hearts are pounding with alarm—how can we further block the gate and stir the crowd?
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered troops to block the Vermilion Bird Gate. Wang Su said: "The emperor is unwell, many dwellings have been crushed, and the people's hearts are pounding with alarm—how can we block the gate and stir them further?"

sentences.zh: 違詔止其役，水亦不害。

translations.literal: Contravening the edict, he stopped the work, and the water did no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Defying the edict, he stopped the work, and the flood did no further harm.

sentences.zh: 出知定州、成都府。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Dingzhou and Chengdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Dingzhou and Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 先是，牙校歲輸酒坊錢以供廚傳，日加厚，輸者轉困。

translations.literal: Previously, military adjutants annually paid wine-monopoly funds to supply official hospitality; the burden grew daily heavier and those who paid grew ever more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, military adjutants had paid wine-monopoly funds annually to supply official hospitality; the burden grew heavier each year and those who paid grew ever more distressed.

sentences.zh: 素一切裁約之。

translations.literal: Su cut back all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su cut back all of it.

sentences.zh: 鐵錢布滿兩蜀，而鼓鑄不止，幣益輕，商賈不行，命罷鑄十年，以權物價。

translations.literal: Iron coins filled both Shu regions, yet minting did not cease; currency grew ever lighter and merchants would not trade; he ordered minting halted for ten years to stabilize prices.
translations.idiomatic: Iron coins flooded both Shu regions, yet minting continued; currency grew lighter and commerce stalled. He ordered minting halted for ten years to stabilize prices.

sentences.zh: 凡為政，務合人情，蜀人紀其目，號曰「王公異斷」。

translations.literal: In all his governance he sought to accord with human feeling; people of Shu recorded his decisions and called them "Lord Wang's Exceptional Judgments."
translations.idiomatic: In all his governance he sought to accord with human feeling; the people of Shu recorded his decisions and called them "Lord Wang's Exceptional Judgments."

sentences.zh: 復知開封。

translations.literal: He again served as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 素以三公子少知名，出入侍從將帥，久頗鞅鞅，厭倦劇煩，事多鹵莽不治，盜賊數發。

translations.literal: Su, as a son of the Three Dukes, had been known from youth; entering and leaving the ranks of attendant officials and generals, over time he grew somewhat discontented, weary of arduous and troublesome affairs; many matters were handled carelessly and left untended, and bandits arose repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: As a son of the Three Dukes, Wang Su had been known from youth; having long moved among attendant officials and generals, he grew discontented and weary of arduous duties; many matters were handled carelessly, and bandits arose repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 御史糾其過，出知許州。

translations.literal: Censors impeached him for his faults and he was sent out as prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censors impeached him for his faults and he was posted as prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 治平初，夏人寇靜邊砦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhiping era, the Tangut people raided Jingbian Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhiping era, the Tangut raided Jingbian Stockade.

sentences.zh: 召拜端明殿學士，復知渭州，於是三鎮、涇原蕃夷故老皆歡賀，比至，敵解去。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and again made prefect of Weizhou; thereupon old men among the tribes of the Three Garrisons and Jingyuan Circuit all rejoiced and congratulated; by the time he arrived, the enemy had withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and again posted to Weizhou, old tribal leaders of the Three Garrisons and Jingyuan Circuit all rejoiced; by the time he arrived, the enemy had withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 拓渭西南城，浚隍三周，積粟支十年。

translations.literal: He expanded the southwestern wall of Weizhou, dredged the moat three circuits deep, and stored grain sufficient for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded Weizhou's southwestern wall, dredged the moat three circuits deep, and stockpiled grain sufficient for ten years.

sentences.zh: 屬羌奉土地來獻，悉增募弓箭手。

translations.literal: Dependent Qiang submitted land as tribute; he increased recruitment of archer militia throughout.
translations.idiomatic: When dependent Qiang submitted land as tribute, he increased recruitment of archer militia throughout.

sentences.zh: 行陳出入之法，身自督訓。

translations.literal: He implemented formation entry and exit methods and personally supervised training.
translations.idiomatic: He implemented formation drill methods and personally supervised training.

sentences.zh: 其居舊穿土為室，寇至，老幼多焚死，為築八堡使居之。

translations.literal: They had formerly dug earth to make dwellings; when raiders came, old and young were often burned to death; he built eight forts for them to live in.
translations.idiomatic: They had formerly dug earthen dwellings; when raiders came, old and young were often burned to death. He built eight forts for them to live in.

sentences.zh: 其從領於兩巡檢，人莫得自便。

translations.literal: Their followers were placed under two patrol inspectors and people could not manage their own affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers were placed under two patrol inspectors, and the people could not manage their own affairs.

sentences.zh: 素曰：「是豈募民兵意邪？」

translations.literal: Su said: "Is this the intent of recruiting militia?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "Is this the intent of recruiting militia?"

sentences.zh: 聽散耕田里，有警則聚，故士氣感奮，精悍他道莫及。

translations.literal: He allowed them to disperse and farm in the fields, gathering when there was alarm; therefore morale was stirred and their fierceness was unmatched in other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed them to disperse and farm in the fields, gathering when alarm came; morale soared, and their fierceness was unmatched in other circuits.

sentences.zh: 嘗宴堂上，邊民傳寇至，驚入城。

translations.literal: Once while feasting in the hall, border people spread word that raiders had come and fled in alarm into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Once while feasting in the hall, border people spread word that raiders had come, and people fled in alarm into the city.

sentences.zh: 諸將曰：「使奸人亦從而入，將必為內應，合拒勿內。」

translations.literal: The generals said: "If treacherous men also enter with them, they will surely serve as inside collaborators; we should refuse them and not let them in.
translations.idiomatic: The generals said: "If treacherous men enter with them, they will serve as inside collaborators; we should refuse them entry."

sentences.zh: 素曰：「若拒之東去，關中必搖。

translations.literal: Su said: "If we refuse them and they flee eastward, the Guanzhong region will surely be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "If we refuse them and they flee eastward, Guanzhong will surely be shaken.

sentences.zh: 吾在此，敵必不敢犯我，此當有奸言。」

translations.literal: While I am here, the enemy will surely not dare attack us; this must be malicious rumor.
translations.idiomatic: While I am here, the enemy will not dare attack us; this must be malicious rumor."

sentences.zh: 乃下令：「敢稱寇至者斬。」

translations.literal: He then issued an order: "Whoever dares say raiders have come shall be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered: "Whoever dares say raiders have come shall be executed."

sentences.zh: 有頃，候騎從西來，人傳果妄，諸將皆服其明。

translations.literal: Before long, scout riders came from the west and people reported that the rumor was indeed false; all the generals admired his clear judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, scout riders came from the west confirming the rumor was false; all the generals admired his clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 換澶州觀察使、知成德軍，改青州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of Chanzhou and prefect of Chengdé Army, then changed to Military Commissioner of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to military commissioner of Chanzhou and prefect of Chengdé Army, he was then changed to military commissioner of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era.

sentences.zh: 還，以學士知太原府。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he served as academician and prefect of Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, he served as academician and prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 汾河大溢，素曰：「若壞平晉，遂灌州城矣。」

translations.literal: The Fen River overflowed greatly; Su said: "If Pingjin is breached, it will then flood the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fen River overflowed, Wang Su said: "If Pingjin is breached, it will flood the prefectural city."

sentences.zh: 亟命具舟楫，築堤以捍之。

translations.literal: He urgently ordered boats and rafts prepared and dikes built to hold it back.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently ordered boats prepared and dikes built to hold it back.

sentences.zh: 一夕，水驟至，人賴以安。

translations.literal: In one night the water suddenly arrived, and the people relied on this to remain safe.
translations.idiomatic: Overnight the flood surged, and the people were saved by his preparations.

sentences.zh: 入知通進銀臺司，轉工部尚書，仍故職致仕。

translations.literal: He entered court as director of the Gateway for Memorials and Silver Terrace Office, was transferred to Minister of Public Works, and retired while retaining his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as director of the Gateway for Memorials and Silver Terrace Office, was transferred to minister of public works, and retired while retaining his former rank.

sentences.zh: 故事，雖三公致仕，亦不帶職。

translations.literal: By precedent, even when the Three Dukes retired, they did not retain office.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, even when the Three Dukes retired, they did not retain office.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方新法制，素首以學士就第。

translations.literal: The court was then instituting new regulations; Su was the first academician to retire to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: As the court instituted new regulations, Wang Su was the first academician to retire to his residence.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十七，諡曰懿敏。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-seven; his posthumous title was Yimin (Dignified and Keen).
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-seven and was granted the posthumous epithet Dignified and Keen.

sentences.zh: 子：鞏；

translations.literal: Son: Gong;
translations.idiomatic: Son: Gong;

sentences.zh: 從子：靖；

translations.literal: Nephew: Jing;
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Jing;

sentences.zh: 從孫：震。

translations.literal: Grandnephew: Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Grandnephew: Zhen.

sentences.zh: 鞏有雋才，長於詩，從蘇軾遊。

translations.literal: Gong had outstanding talent, excelled in poetry, and associated with Su Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had outstanding talent, excelled in poetry, and associated with Su Shi.

sentences.zh: 軾守徐州，鞏往訪之，與客遊泗水，登魋山，吹笛飲酒，乘月而歸。

translations.literal: When Shi was prefect of Xuzhou, Gong went to visit him; with guests he toured the Si River, climbed Mount Gui, played the flute and drank wine, and returned by moonlight.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was prefect of Xuzhou, Gong visited him; with guests he toured the Si River, climbed Mount Gui, played the flute and drank wine, and returned by moonlight.

sentences.zh: 軾待之於黃樓上，謂鞏曰：「李太白死，世無此樂三百年矣。」

translations.literal: Shi received him at the Yellow Tower and said to Gong: "Since Li Taibai died, the world has had no such pleasure for three hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi received him at the Yellow Tower and said to Gong: "Since Li Bai died, the world has had no such pleasure for three hundred years.

sentences.zh: 軾得罪，鞏亦竄賓州。

translations.literal: When Shi was punished, Gong was also banished to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was punished, Gong was also banished to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 數歲得還，豪氣不少挫。

translations.literal: After several years he was allowed to return, and his bold spirit was little diminished.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was allowed to return, and his bold spirit was little diminished.

sentences.zh: 後歷宗正丞，以跌蕩傲世，每除官，輒為言者所議，故終不顯。

translations.literal: Later he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court; because he was unrestrained and proud toward the world, whenever he was appointed to office, remonstrators would criticize it, and therefore he never achieved prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as vice director of the Imperial Clan Court; unrestrained and proud, he was criticized whenever appointed to office and never achieved prominence.

sentences.zh: 從子 靖

translations.literal: Nephew: Jing
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Jing

sentences.zh: 靖，字詹叔，蚤孤，自力於學，好講切天下利害。

translations.literal: Jing, styled Zhanshu, lost his father early, exerted himself in study, and loved to discuss the benefits and harms of affairs throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, courtesy name Zhanshu, lost his father early, applied himself to study, and loved to discuss the benefits and harms of affairs throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 以祖蔭歷通判閬州、知滁州，主管北京御史臺。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather's privilege he served successively as vice-prefect of Langzhou, prefect of Chuzhou, and supervisor of the Beijing Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Through his grandfather's privilege he served as vice-prefect of Langzhou, prefect of Chuzhou, and supervisor of the Beijing Censorate.

sentences.zh: 契丹數遣橫使來，靖疏言：「彼利中國賜遺，挾虛聲以濟其欲，漸不可長，宜有以折之。」

translations.literal: The Khitan repeatedly sent cross-border envoys; Jing submitted a memorial saying: "They profit from China's gifts and tribute, wielding empty threats to satisfy their desires; this cannot be allowed to grow; we should have means to check them.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan repeatedly sent cross-border envoys. Jing memorialized: "They profit from Song gifts and tribute, wielding empty threats to satisfy their desires; this cannot be allowed to grow—we should find means to check them."

sentences.zh: 又請復明經科，加試貢士以策，觀其所學，稍變聲律之習。

translations.literal: He also requested restoration of the Classics Examination, adding policy essays for presented scholars to observe their learning and gradually change the habit of tonal prosody.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to restore the Classics Examination and add policy essays for presented scholars, to observe their learning and gradually change the habit of tonal prosody.

sentences.zh: 擢利州路轉運判官，提點陝西刑獄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Transport Assessor of Lizhou Circuit and Investigating Commissioner of Shaanxi Judicial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to transport assessor of Lizhou Circuit and investigating commissioner of Shaanxi judicial affairs.

sentences.zh: 鄉戶役於州縣者，優則願久留，勞則欲亟去，吏得權其遲速。

translations.literal: Households serving corvée at prefectures and counties, when treated well wished to stay long, when overworked wished to leave quickly, and clerks could control whether they stayed or went.
translations.idiomatic: Households serving corvée at prefectures and counties, when treated well wished to stay, when overworked wished to leave quickly, and clerks controlled whether they stayed or went.

sentences.zh: 靖一以歲月遣代，遂為令。

translations.literal: Jing uniformly dispatched replacements by fixed terms of months and years, and this became regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Jing uniformly dispatched replacements by fixed terms, and this became regulation.

sentences.zh: 徙河東長子縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Changzi County in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Changzi County in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 賊殺人，捕治十數輩，不得實，皆釋去。

translations.literal: Bandits killed someone; more than ten persons were arrested and tried but the truth could not be found, and all were released.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits killed someone, more than ten suspects were arrested but the truth could not be found, and all were released.

sentences.zh: 靖閱其牘曰：「此真盜也。」

translations.literal: Jing reviewed the dossier and said: "This is the real thief.
translations.idiomatic: Jing reviewed the dossier and said: "This is the real thief."

sentences.zh: 教吏曲折訊囚，果服罪。

translations.literal: He instructed clerks to interrogate the prisoner by indirect means, and the man indeed confessed.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed clerks to interrogate the prisoner by indirect means, and the man confessed.

sentences.zh: 為開封府推官。

translations.literal: He served as judicial aide of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial aide of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曹、濮盜害，官吏久不獲，靖受詔督捕，成擒者十八九。

translations.literal: Bandits ravaged Cao and Pu prefectures; officials had long failed to capture them; Jing received an edict to supervise the hunt and captured eight or nine tenths of them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits ravaged Cao and Pu prefectures and officials had long failed to capture them, Jing received an edict to supervise the hunt and captured eight or nine tenths of them.

sentences.zh: 因言盜之不戢，由大姓為囊橐，請並坐之，著為令。

translations.literal: He then said that bandits were not restrained because great clans served as their storehouses; he asked that they be punished together and this be established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that bandits went unchecked because great clans sheltered them; he asked that they be punished together and this be established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 徙廣南轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Transport Commissioner of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to transport commissioner of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，廣人訛言交阯且至，老幼入保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xining era, people of Guang spread false rumors that Jiaozhi was about to arrive, and old and young fled into stockades.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era, people of Guang spread false rumors that Jiaozhi was about to invade, and old and young fled into stockades.

sentences.zh: 事聞，中外以為憂。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, court and commonwealth alike regarded it with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, court and country alike regarded it with alarm.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「王靖在彼，可無念。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong said: "With Wang Jing there, there is no need for concern.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong said: "With Wang Jing there, there is no need for concern."

sentences.zh: 即拜太常少卿、直昭文館、知廣州。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed directly to the Hall of Illustrious Culture, and made prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed directly to the Hall of Illustrious Culture, and made prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 居二年，入為度支副使，卒。

translations.literal: After two years he entered court as Vice Commissioner of Revenue and died.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he entered court as vice commissioner of revenue and died.

sentences.zh: 子古，字敏仲，第進士。

translations.literal: His son Gu, styled Minzhong, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu, courtesy name Minzhong, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，為司農主簿，使行淮、浙振旱菑，究張若濟獄，劾轉運使王廷老、張靚失職，皆罷之。

translations.literal: During the Xining era he served as chief clerk of the Ministry of Revenue; he was dispatched to Huai and Zhe to relieve drought famine, investigated the Zhang Ruoji case, impeached transport commissioners Wang Tinglao and Zhang Jing for neglect of duty, and all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he served as chief clerk of the Ministry of Revenue, was dispatched to Huai and Zhe to relieve drought famine, investigated the Zhang Ruoji case, impeached transport commissioners Wang Tinglao and Zhang Jing for neglect of duty, and all were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 連提舉四路常平，王安禮欲用為太常丞，神宗謂古好異論，止以為博士。

translations.literal: He successively supervised the Ever-Normal Granaries of four circuits; Wang Anli wished to appoint him Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but Emperor Shenzong said Gu loved unorthodox opinions and made him only a erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He successively supervised the Ever-Normal Granaries of four circuits. Wang Anli wished to appoint him vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but Emperor Shenzong said Gu loved unorthodox opinions and made him only an erudite.

sentences.zh: 加上仁宗、英宗諡，因升祔四后，初議不發冊，古言：「發冊之禮，雖為祔廟節文，而升祔之重，乃由冊而後顯。

translations.literal: When posthumous titles were added for Emperors Renzong and Yingzong and four empresses were elevated for joint enshrinement, the initial plan was not to issue registers; Gu said: "The rite of issuing registers, though a detail of joint enshrinement, is what makes the weight of elevation visible through the register.
translations.idiomatic: When posthumous titles were added for Emperors Renzong and Yingzong and four empresses were elevated for joint enshrinement, the initial plan was not to issue registers. Gu said: "The rite of issuing registers, though a detail of joint enshrinement, is what makes the weight of elevation visible through the register.

sentences.zh: 今既行升祔，則禮不可廢。」

translations.literal: Now that joint enshrinement is being carried out, the rite cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Now that joint enshrinement is being carried out, the rite cannot be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 乃詔用竹冊。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon ordered the use of bamboo registers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon ordered the use of bamboo registers.

sentences.zh: 又定諸神祠封額、爵號之序。

translations.literal: He also fixed the order of enfeoffment titles and noble ranks for spirit shrines.
translations.idiomatic: He also fixed the order of enfeoffment titles and noble ranks for spirit shrines.

sentences.zh: 出為湖南轉運判官，提點淮東刑獄，歷工部、吏部、右司員外郎，太府少卿。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Transport Assessor of Hunan, Investigating Commissioner of Huaidong Judicial Affairs, and served successively as Assistant Director in the Ministries of Public Works and Personnel, the Right Office, and as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as transport assessor of Hunan and investigating commissioner of Huaidong judicial affairs, he served successively as assistant director in the ministries of public works and personnel, the Right Office, and as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，異時北使所過，凡供張悉貸於民，古請出公錢為之，民得不擾。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan, formerly wherever northern envoys passed, all provisions were levied from the people; Gu requested that public funds be used instead, and the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Khitan, formerly wherever northern envoys passed, all provisions were levied from the people. Gu requested that public funds be used instead, and the people were not disturbed.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，遷戶部侍郎，詳定役法，與尚書蔡京多不合。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, detailed to revise the corvée law, and often disagreed with Minister Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era he was promoted to vice minister of revenue, detailed to revise the corvée law, and often disagreed with Minister Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 京言：「臣欲用元豐人額雇直，而古乃用司馬光法。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "I wish to use the Yuanfeng quota hire rates, yet Gu uses Sima Guang's method.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing said: "I wish to use the Yuanfeng quota hire rates, yet Gu uses Sima Guang's method."

sentences.zh: 詔徙古兵部，尋以集賢殿修撰為江淮發運使，進寶文閣待制、知廣州。
