translations.literal: An edict transferred Gu to the Ministry of War; soon after, as Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he served as Transport Commissioner of the Jiang-Huai region, was promoted to Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Precious Culture, and made prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict transferred Gu to the Ministry of War; soon after, as compiler of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he served as transport commissioner of the Jiang-Huai region, was promoted to awaiting draftsman of the Hall of Precious Culture, and made prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者論其常指平歲為凶年，妄散邦財，奪職知袁州。

translations.literal: Remonstrators argued that he habitually treated normal years as famine years and recklessly dispersed state funds; he was stripped of office and made prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators argued that he habitually treated normal years as famine years and recklessly dispersed state funds; he was stripped of office and posted as prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，復拜戶部侍郎，遷尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, Gu was again appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended, Gu was again appointed vice minister of revenue and promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 與御史中丞趙挺之偕領放欠，挺之言：「古蠲除太多，欲盡傾天下之財，不可用。」

translations.literal: Together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Tingzhi he jointly supervised debt remission; Tingzhi said: "Gu remits too much and wishes to drain all the wealth under heaven; he cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: Together with vice censor-in-chief Zhao Tingzhi he jointly supervised debt remission. Tingzhi said: "Gu remits too much and wishes to drain all the wealth under heaven; he cannot be used."

sentences.zh: 遂改刑部。

translations.literal: He was thereupon transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 攻不已，以寶文閣直學士知成都。

translations.literal: As attacks continued, he was made Academician Directly Attached to the Hall of Precious Culture and prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: As attacks continued, he was made academician of the Hall of Precious Culture and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 墮崇寧黨籍，責衡州別駕，安置溫州。

translations.literal: He fell into the Chongning faction register, was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Hengzhou, and assigned to Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fell into the Chongning faction register, was demoted to assistant administrator of Hengzhou, and assigned to Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 復朝散郎，尋卒。

translations.literal: He was restored to Gentleman for Court Discussion and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to gentleman for court discussion and soon died.

sentences.zh: 從孫 震

translations.literal: Grandnephew: Zhen
translations.idiomatic: Grandnephew: Zhen

sentences.zh: 震，字子發，以父任試銓優等，賜及第。

translations.literal: Zhen, styled Zifa, through his father's privilege passed the examination bureau with superior grade and was granted examination success.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, courtesy name Zifa, through his father's privilege passed the examination bureau with superior grade and was granted examination success.

sentences.zh: 上諸路學制，神宗稱其才。

translations.literal: He submitted the school system for all circuits; Emperor Shenzong praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the school system for all circuits; Emperor Shenzong praised his talent.

sentences.zh: 以習學中書刑房公事，遂為檢正。

translations.literal: Through study of the criminal affairs section of the Secretariat, he became a rectifying official.
translations.idiomatic: Through study of the criminal affairs section of the Secretariat, he became a rectifying official.

sentences.zh: 預修條例，加館閣校勘，檢正孔目吏房。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling regulations, was added as collator in the Imperial Archives, and served as rectifying official of the Personnel and Accounts Section.
translations.idiomatic: He participated in compiling regulations, was added as collator in the Imperial Archives, and served as rectifying official of the Personnel and Accounts Section.

sentences.zh: 元豐官制行，震與吳雍從輔臣執筆入記上語，面授尚書右司員外郎，使自書除目，舉朝榮之。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng bureaucratic system was implemented, Zhen and Wu Yong followed the chief ministers with brush in hand to record the Emperor's words; he was personally appointed Assistant Director of the Right Office of the Ministry and ordered to write his own appointment edict himself—the whole court honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng bureaucratic system was implemented, Zhen and Wu Yong followed the chief ministers with brush in hand to record the emperor's words; he was personally appointed assistant director of the Right Office and ordered to write his own appointment edict—the whole court honored him.

sentences.zh: 兼修《市易敕》，帝諭之曰：「朝廷造法，皆本先王之制，推行非人，故不能善後。

translations.literal: Concurrently compiling the "Market Exchange Edict," the Emperor instructed him: "When the court creates laws, all are based on the institutions of former kings; when implementation is entrusted to the wrong men, good results cannot follow.
translations.idiomatic: While compiling the Market Exchange Edict, the emperor instructed him: "When the court creates laws, all are based on the institutions of former kings; when implementation is entrusted to the wrong men, good results cannot follow.

sentences.zh: 且以錢貸民，有不能償，輒籍其家，豈善政也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when money is lent to the people and they cannot repay, their households are immediately confiscated—is this good governance?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when money is lent to the people and they cannot repay, their households are immediately confiscated—is this good governance?

sentences.zh: 宜計其負幾何，悉捐之。」

translations.literal: You should calculate how much is owed and remit it all.
translations.idiomatic: Calculate how much is owed and remit it all.

sentences.zh: 震頓首奉詔。

translations.literal: Zhen bowed his head and received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen bowed and received the edict.

sentences.zh: 進起居舍人，使行西邊，還為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Daily Record Attendant, dispatched on a mission to the western border, and on return became Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to daily record attendant, dispatched on a mission to the western border, he returned as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，遷給事中，御史王岩叟劾之，以龍圖閣待制知蔡州，歷五郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was promoted to Supervising Attendant; Censor Wang Yansou impeached him and he was made Awaiting Draftsman of the Dragon Designs Pavilion and prefect of Caizhou, serving in five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he was promoted to supervising attendant; censor Wang Yansou impeached him and he was made awaiting draftsman of the Dragon Designs Pavilion and prefect of Caizhou, serving in five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，復為給事中，權吏部尚書，拜龍圖閣直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era he again served as Supervising Attendant, acted as Minister of Personnel, and was appointed Academician Directly Attached to the Dragon Designs Pavilion and prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shaosheng era he again served as supervising attendant, acted as minister of personnel, and was appointed academician of the Dragon Designs Pavilion and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 震與章惇皆呂惠卿所薦，而素不相能。

translations.literal: Zhen and Zhang Dun were both recommended by Lü Huiqing, yet had never gotten along.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and Zhang Dun were both recommended by Lü Huiqing, yet had never gotten along.

sentences.zh: 府奏獄空，哲宗疑不實。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported empty prisons; Emperor Zhezong suspected this was untrue.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported empty prisons; Emperor Zhezong suspected this was untrue.

sentences.zh: 震謂惇抑已，於是潁昌蓋漸有訟，許賂惇子弟，震捕漸掠治，頗得蹤跡。

translations.literal: Zhen believed Dun was suppressing him; thereupon in Yingchang a man named Gai gradually came under litigation, having promised bribes to Dun's sons and nephews; Zhen arrested Gai and interrogated him by degrees, obtaining considerable traces of evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen believed Dun was suppressing him; thereupon in Yingchang a man named Gai came under litigation, having promised bribes to Dun's sons and nephews; Zhen arrested Gai and interrogated him, obtaining considerable evidence.

sentences.zh: 惇懼，以獄付大理，而徙震為樞密都承旨，遂坐折獄滋蔓、傾搖大臣，奪職知岳州，卒。

translations.literal: Dun grew afraid and transferred the case to the Court of Judicial Review, while Zhen was moved to Chief Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he was then punished for letting the case spread and shake grand ministers, stripped of office and made prefect of Yuezhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Dun grew afraid and transferred the case to the Court of Judicial Review, while Zhen was moved to chief coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs; he was then punished for letting the case spread and implicate grand ministers, stripped of office and posted to Yuezhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 余靖，字安道，韶州曲江人。

translations.literal: Yu Jing, styled Andao, was a native of Qujiang in Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing, courtesy name Andao, was a native of Qujiang in Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 少不事羈檢，以文學稱鄉里。

translations.literal: In youth he did not submit to restraint, and was renowned in his home district for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he did not submit to restraint and was renowned in his home district for literary learning.

sentences.zh: 舉進士起家，為贛縣尉，試書判拔萃，改將作監丞、知新建縣，遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: Passing the jinshi examination he began his career as magistrate of Gan County; excelling in the document-judgment examination, he was changed to Director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories and prefect of Xinjian County, and promoted to Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the jinshi examination he began his career as magistrate of Gan County; excelling in the document-judgment examination, he was changed to director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories and prefect of Xinjian County, and promoted to secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 數上書論事，建言班固《漢書》舛謬，命與王洙並校司馬遷、范曄二史。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials discussing affairs, proposed that Ban Gu's Book of Han contained errors, and was ordered together with Wang Zhu to collate the histories of Sima Qian and Fan Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted memorials discussing affairs, proposed that Ban Gu's Book of Han contained errors, and was ordered together with Wang Zhu to collate the histories of Sima Qian and Fan Ye.

sentences.zh: 書奏，擢集賢校理。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was promoted to Collator of the Academy of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he was promoted to collator of the Academy of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹貶饒州，諫官御史莫敢言。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan was demoted to Raozhou; remonstrance officials and censors dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan was demoted to Raozhou, remonstrance officials and censors dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 靖言：「仲淹以刺譏大臣重加譴謫，倘其言未合聖慮，在陛下聽與不聽耳，安可以為罪乎？

translations.literal: Jing said: "Zhongyan was heavily punished and demoted for criticizing grand ministers; if his words did not accord with Your Majesty's intent, that lies in whether Your Majesty listens or not—how can this be made a crime?
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing said: "Zhongyan was heavily punished for criticizing grand ministers; if his words did not accord with Your Majesty's intent, that lies in whether Your Majesty listens or not—how can this be made a crime?

sentences.zh: 汲黯在廷，以平津為多詐；

translations.literal: Ji An was at court and called Lord Pingjin deceitful;
translations.idiomatic: Ji An was at court and called Lord Pingjin deceitful;

sentences.zh: 張昭論將，以魯肅為粗疏。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao discussed generals and called Lu Su crude and careless.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao discussed generals and called Lu Su crude and careless.

sentences.zh: 漢皇、吳主熟聞訾毀，兩用無猜，豈損令德。

translations.literal: The Han emperor and the Wu ruler often heard such slander yet employed both men without suspicion—did this harm their fine virtue?
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor and the Wu ruler often heard such criticism yet employed both men without suspicion—did this harm their fine virtue?

sentences.zh: 陛下自親政以來，屢逐言事者，恐鉗天下口，不可。」

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty personally assumed governance, remonstrators have been repeatedly dismissed; I fear this will clamp shut the mouths of all under heaven—this cannot be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty personally assumed governance, remonstrators have been repeatedly dismissed; I fear this will clamp shut the mouths of all under heaven—this cannot be allowed.

sentences.zh: 疏入，落職監筠州酒稅。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was stripped of office and made supervisor of wine taxes at Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, he was stripped of office and made supervisor of wine taxes at Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 尹洙、歐陽修亦以仲淹故，相繼貶逐，靖繇是益知名。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu and Ouyang Xiu were also demoted and banished on Zhongyan's account; Jing thereby grew all the more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu and Ouyang Xiu were also demoted and banished on Zhongyan's account; Yu Jing thereby grew all the more renowned.

sentences.zh: 徙監泰州稅，知英州，遷太常博士，復為校理、同知禮院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervise taxes at Taizhou, served as prefect of Yingzhou, was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and again served as collator and Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to supervise taxes at Taizhou, he served as prefect of Yingzhou, was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and again served as collator and associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，仁宗銳意欲更天下敝事，增諫官員，使論得失，以靖為右正言。

translations.literal: During the Qingli era, Emperor Renzong was keen to reform the corrupt affairs of all under heaven, increased remonstrance officials to discuss gains and losses, and appointed Jing as Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era, Emperor Renzong was keen to reform corrupt affairs throughout the realm, increased remonstrance officials to discuss policy, and appointed Yu Jing as right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 時四方盜賊竊發，州郡不能制。

translations.literal: At the time bandits arose in secret throughout the four directions and prefectures and circuits could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits arose throughout the realm and prefectures and circuits could not control them.

sentences.zh: 靖言：「朝廷威制天下在賞罰，今官吏弛事，群盜蜂起，大臣齷齪守常，不立法禁，可為國家憂也。

translations.literal: Jing said: "The court's authority over all under heaven lies in rewards and punishments; now officials neglect their duties, bandits swarm like bees, grand ministers are petty and cling to routine, and no laws or prohibitions are established—this is cause for the state's alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing said: "The court's authority over the realm lies in rewards and punishments; now officials neglect their duties, bandits swarm, grand ministers are petty and cling to routine, and no laws or prohibitions are established—this is cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 請嚴捕賊賞罰，及定為賊劫質、亡失器甲除名追官之法。」

translations.literal: I ask that rewards and punishments for capturing bandits be made strict, and that laws be fixed for stripping names and ranks when bandits seize hostages or when armor and weapons are lost.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that rewards and punishments for capturing bandits be made strict, and that laws be fixed for stripping names and ranks when bandits seize hostages or when armor and weapons are lost."

sentences.zh: 司天言太白犯歲星，又犯執法。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy reported that Venus had encroached upon Jupiter and also encroached upon the asterism Zhifa.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Astronomy reported that Venus had encroached upon Jupiter and also upon the asterism Zhifa.

sentences.zh: 靖上疏請責躬修德，以謝天變。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a memorial asking that the Emperor examine himself and cultivate virtue to respond to Heaven's changes.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing submitted a memorial asking that the emperor examine himself and cultivate virtue to respond to Heaven's changes.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，辭日，以所奏事書笏，各舉一字為目，凡數十事。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan, on the day of his farewell audience he wrote his memorial matters on his court tablet, taking one character from each as a heading—several dozen matters in all.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Khitan, at his farewell audience he wrote his memorial matters on his court tablet, taking one character from each as a heading—several dozen matters in all.

sentences.zh: 帝顧見之，命悉條奏，日幾昃，乃罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor glanced and saw it, ordered that all be submitted item by item, and only when the sun was nearly setting did he dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor glanced and saw it, ordered that all be submitted item by item, and only when the sun was nearly setting did he dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 進修起居注。

translations.literal: He was promoted to compile the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to compile the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 開寶寺靈感塔災，復上疏言：「五行之占，本是災變，朝廷所宜誡懼，以答天意。

translations.literal: When the Spirit Response Pagoda of Kaibao Temple suffered a fire, he again submitted a memorial saying: "Divinations of the Five Phases are fundamentally portents of disaster and change; the court ought to be warned and fearful to respond to Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Spirit Response Pagoda of Kaibao Temple burned, he again submitted a memorial: "Divinations of the Five Phases are portents of disaster; the court ought to be warned and fearful to respond to Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 聞嘗詔取舊瘞舍利入禁中閱視，道路傳言，舍利在內廷有光怪，竊恐巧佞之人，推為靈異，惑亂視聽，再圖營造。

translations.literal: I hear that an edict once ordered old buried relics taken into the inner palace for inspection; rumors spread on the roads that the relics in the inner court emitted strange lights; I secretly fear that artful and sycophantic men will promote them as miraculous, confusing sight and hearing, and again plan construction.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that an edict once ordered old buried relics brought into the inner palace for inspection; rumors spread that the relics in the inner court emitted strange lights; I fear that artful sycophants will promote them as miraculous, confusing the court, and again plan construction.

sentences.zh: 臣聞帝王之道，能勤儉厥德，感動人心，則雖有危難，後必安濟。

translations.literal: I have heard that the way of emperors and kings is that if one can be diligent and frugal in virtue and move people's hearts, then though there be danger and hardship, peace will surely follow afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The way of emperors and kings is that if one is diligent and frugal in virtue and moves people's hearts, then though there be danger and hardship, peace will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 今自西垂用兵，國帑虛竭，民亡儲蓄，十室九空。

translations.literal: Now since war on the western frontier, the state treasury is empty and exhausted, the people have lost their savings, and nine of ten households stand vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Since war on the western frontier, the state treasury is empty, the people have lost their savings, and nine of ten households stand vacant.

sentences.zh: 陛下若勤勞罪己，憂人之憂，則四民安居，海內蒙福。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty labors diligently, takes blame upon yourself, and shares the people's worries, then the four classes of people will dwell in peace and all within the seas will receive blessing.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty labors diligently, takes blame upon yourself, and shares the people's worries, then the four classes of people will dwell in peace and the realm will receive blessing.

sentences.zh: 如不恤民病，廣事浮費，奉佛求福，非天下所望也。

translations.literal: If you do not care for the people's afflictions, widely undertake wasteful expenditures, and seek fortune through Buddhism, this is not what all under heaven hope for.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not care for the people's afflictions, undertake wasteful expenditures, and seek fortune through Buddhism, this is not what the realm hopes for.

sentences.zh: 若以舍利經火不壞，遽為神異，即本在土中，火所不及。

translations.literal: If because the relics were unharmed by fire they are suddenly deemed miraculous, they were originally in the earth where fire could not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: If because the relics were unharmed by fire they are suddenly deemed miraculous, they were originally in the earth where fire could not reach them.

sentences.zh: 若言舍利皆能出光怪，必有神靈憑之，此妄言也。

translations.literal: If one says all relics can emit strange lights, there must be spirits dwelling in them—this is false talk.
translations.idiomatic: If one says all relics can emit strange lights, there must be spirits dwelling in them—this is false talk.

sentences.zh: 且一塔不能自衛，為火所毀，況藉其福以庇民哉？」

translations.literal: Moreover, a single pagoda could not protect itself and was destroyed by fire—how much less could one rely on its blessing to shelter the people?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a single pagoda could not protect itself and was destroyed by fire—how much less could one rely on its blessing to shelter the people?"

sentences.zh: 靖在職數言事，嘗論夏竦奸邪，不可為樞密使；

translations.literal: Jing repeatedly spoke on affairs in office; he once argued that Xia Song was wicked and treacherous and could not serve as Military Affairs Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing repeatedly spoke on affairs in office; he once argued that Xia Song was wicked and treacherous and could not serve as military affairs commissioner;

sentences.zh: 王舉正不才，不宜在政府；

translations.literal: Wang Juzheng was without talent and was unsuited for the government;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Juzheng was without talent and was unsuited for the government;

sentences.zh: 狄青武人，使之獨守渭州，恐敗邊事；

translations.literal: Di Qing was a military man; to have him alone guard Weizhou might ruin border affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing was a military man; to have him alone guard Weizhou might ruin border affairs;

sentences.zh: 張堯佐以修媛故，除提點府界公事，非政事之美，且郭后之禍，起於楊、尚，不可不監。

translations.literal: Zhang Yaozuo, on account of Lady Xiu, was appointed Supervisor of Capital-District Affairs—not a fine matter of governance; moreover, the calamity of Empress Guo arose from Lady Yang and Lady Shang—this must be taken as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yaozuo, on account of Lady Xiu, was appointed supervisor of capital-district affairs—not a fine matter of governance; moreover, the calamity of Empress Guo arose from Lady Yang and Lady Shang—this must be taken as a warning.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王翼西京治獄還，賜五品服，靖曰：「治獄而錫服，外人不知，必以為翼深文重法，能希陛下意，以取此寵，所損非細事也。

translations.literal: Erudite Wang Yi of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices returned from handling cases in the Western Capital and was granted fifth-rank robes; Jing said: "To grant robes for handling cases—outsiders will not know and will surely think Yi applied harsh laws and heavy penalties, able to guess Your Majesty's intent to win this favor; the harm is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Yi of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices returned from handling cases in the Western Capital and was granted fifth-rank robes. Yu Jing said: "To grant robes for handling cases—outsiders will think Yi applied harsh laws to win Your Majesty's favor; the harm is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 嘗有工部郎中呂覺以治獄賜對，祈易章綬，陛下諭之曰：『朕不欲因鞫囚與人恩澤。』

translations.literal: Once Bureau Director Lü Jue of the Ministry of Public Works was granted an audience for handling cases and requested a change of insignia; Your Majesty instructed him: 'I do not wish to bestow grace upon men because of interrogating prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Once bureau director Lü Jue of the Ministry of Public Works was granted an audience for handling cases and requested a change of insignia; Your Majesty instructed him: 'I do not wish to bestow grace upon men because of interrogating prisoners.

sentences.zh: 覺退以告臣，臣嘗書之起居注。

translations.literal: Jue withdrew and told me; I once recorded this in the Daily Record.
translations.idiomatic: Jue withdrew and told me; I recorded this in the Daily Record.

sentences.zh: 陛下前日諭覺是，則今日賜翼非矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's instruction to Jue the other day was right; then today's grant to Yi is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's instruction to Jue the other day was right; then today's grant to Yi is wrong.

sentences.zh: 是非與奪之間，貴乎一體。

translations.literal: Between right and wrong, grant and denial, what is valued is consistency.
translations.idiomatic: Between right and wrong, grant and denial, what is valued is consistency.

sentences.zh: 小人望風希進，無所不至，幸陛下每於事端，抑其奔競。」

translations.literal: Petty men watch the wind and hope for advancement, reaching everywhere; I hope Your Majesty will at every turn of affairs restrain their scrambling for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men watch the wind and hope for advancement; I hope Your Majesty will at every turn of affairs restrain their scrambling for promotion.

sentences.zh: 其說多見納用。

translations.literal: Many of his proposals were accepted and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his proposals were accepted and implemented.

sentences.zh: 會西鄙厭兵，元昊請和，議增歲賜。

translations.literal: Just as the western frontier grew weary of war, Yuan Hao requested peace, and there was discussion of increasing the annual gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the western frontier grew weary of war, Yuan Hao requested peace, and there was discussion of increasing the annual gifts.

sentences.zh: 靖言：「景德中，契丹舉國興師，直抵澶淵，先帝北征渡河，止捐金繒三十萬與之。

translations.literal: Jing said: "In the Jingde era, the Khitan mobilized the entire nation and marched straight to Chanyuan; the late Emperor personally led a northern expedition across the river and gave them only three hundred thousand in gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing said: "In the Jingde era, the Khitan mobilized the entire nation and marched straight to Chanyuan; Emperor Zhenzong personally led a northern expedition across the river and gave them only three hundred thousand in gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 今元昊戰雖累勝，皆由將帥輕敵易動之故。

translations.literal: Today Yuan Hao has won battle after battle, all because generals underestimated the enemy and acted rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Today Yuan Hao has won battle after battle, all because generals underestimated the enemy and acted rashly.

sentences.zh: 數年選將練兵，始知守戰之備，而銳意解仇，所予至二十六萬。

translations.literal: For several years generals were selected and troops trained before defensive and offensive preparations were known; yet now, eager to settle the feud, what is offered reaches two hundred and sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: For several years generals were selected and troops trained before defensive preparations were in place; yet now, eager to settle the feud, what is offered reaches two hundred and sixty thousand.

sentences.zh: 且戎事有機，國力有限，失之於始，雖悔何追。

translations.literal: Border affairs have their moment, and state strength has its limits; lose at the start, and though one regrets, what can be recovered?
translations.idiomatic: Border affairs have their moment, and state strength has its limits; lose at the start, and no recovery is possible.

sentences.zh: 夫以景德之患，近在封域之內，而歲賜如彼；

translations.literal: The Jingde calamity was close, within the borders themselves, yet annual gifts were as they were;
translations.idiomatic: The Jingde calamity was close, within the borders themselves, yet annual gifts were as they were;

sentences.zh: 今日之警，遠在邊鄙之外，而歲賜如此。

translations.literal: today's alarm is far beyond the frontier, yet annual gifts are like this.
translations.idiomatic: today's alarm is far beyond the frontier, yet annual gifts are like this.

sentences.zh: 若元昊使還，益有所許，契丹聞之，寧不生心？

translations.literal: If when Yuan Hao's envoy returns he is granted still more, when the Khitan hear of it, will they not take heart?
translations.idiomatic: If when Yuan Hao's envoy returns he is granted still more, when the Khitan hear of it, will they not take heart?

sentences.zh: 無厭之求，自此始矣。

translations.literal: Insatiable demands begin from this.
translations.idiomatic: Insatiable demands begin from this.

sentences.zh: 儻移西而備北，為禍更深。

translations.literal: If forces shift west to guard the north, the calamity will be deeper still.
translations.idiomatic: If forces shift west to guard the north, the calamity will be deeper still.

sentences.zh: 但思和與不和，皆有後患，則不必曲意俯徇，以貽國羞。」

translations.literal: But consider that whether there is peace or not, there are consequences either way—then there is no need to bend and defer, bringing shame upon the state.
translations.idiomatic: But consider that whether there is peace or not, there are consequences either way—then there is no need to bend and defer, bringing shame upon the state.

sentences.zh: 擢知制誥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to draftsman of edicts.

sentences.zh: 元昊既歸款，朝廷欲加封冊，而契丹以兵臨西境，遣使言：「為中國討賊，請止毋和。」

translations.literal: After Yuan Hao submitted allegiance, the court wished to bestow enfeoffment, but the Khitan massed troops on the western border and sent envoys saying: "We are punishing the bandits for China; please stop and do not make peace.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao submitted allegiance, the court wished to bestow enfeoffment, but the Khitan massed troops on the western border and sent envoys saying: "We are punishing the bandits for China; please stop and do not make peace.

sentences.zh: 朝議難之。

translations.literal: Court discussion found this difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion found this difficult.

sentences.zh: 會靖數言契丹挾詐，不可輕許，即遣靖往報，而留夏國封策不發。

translations.literal: Just then Jing repeatedly said the Khitan were wielding deception and could not be lightly conceded to; he was immediately dispatched to report back, while the Western Xia enfeoffment edict was held back.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yu Jing repeatedly said the Khitan were wielding deception and could not be lightly conceded to; he was immediately dispatched to report back, while the Western Xia enfeoffment edict was held back.

sentences.zh: 靖至契丹，卒屈其議而還。

translations.literal: When Jing reached the Khitan, he ultimately forced them to yield on the issue and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jing reached the Khitan, he ultimately forced them to yield on the issue and returned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遂發夏冊，臣元昊。

translations.literal: The court thereupon issued the Western Xia enfeoffment and enfeoffed Yuan Hao.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon issued the Western Xia enfeoffment and enfeoffed Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 西師既解嚴，北邊亦無事。

translations.literal: The western armies were relieved from alert, and the northern border was also without incident.
translations.idiomatic: The western armies were relieved from alert, and the northern border was also without incident.

sentences.zh: 靖三使契丹，亦習外國語，嘗為番語詩，御史王平等劾靖失使者體，出知吉州。

translations.literal: Jing went on three missions to the Khitan and also learned foreign languages; he once composed a poem in the barbarian tongue; Censor Wang Ping and others impeached him for failing the dignity of an envoy and he was sent out as prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing went on three missions to the Khitan and also learned foreign languages; he once composed a poem in the barbarian tongue; censor Wang Ping and others impeached him for failing the dignity of an envoy and he was posted as prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 靖為諫官時，嘗劾奏太常博士茹孝標不孝，匿母喪，坐廢。

translations.literal: When Jing was a remonstrance official, he once impeached Erudite Ru Xiaobiao of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for filial impiety, concealing his mother's death, and Ru was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jing was a remonstrance official, he once impeached erudite Ru Xiaobiao of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for filial impiety, concealing his mother's death, and Ru was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 靖既失勢，孝標詣闕言靖少遊廣州，犯法受榜。

translations.literal: After Jing lost influence, Xiaobiao came to court and said Jing in youth had traveled in Guangzhou and violated the law, receiving beating punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Jing lost influence, Xiaobiao came to court and said Jing in youth had traveled in Guangzhou and violated the law, receiving beating punishment.

sentences.zh: 靖聞之不自得，求侍養去。

translations.literal: When Jing heard of this he was ill at ease and requested leave to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jing heard of this he was ill at ease and requested leave to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 改將作少監，分司南京，居曲江。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories and assigned to branch service at the Southern Capital, residing in Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to vice director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories and assigned to branch service at the Southern Capital, residing in Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 已而授左神武軍大將軍、雅州刺史、壽州兵馬鈐轄，辭不就。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army, Prefect of Yazhou, and Military Coordinator of Shouzhou, but he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed grand general of the Left Divine Martial Army, prefect of Yazhou, and military coordinator of Shouzhou, but he declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 再遷衛尉卿、知虔州，丁父憂去。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made prefect of Qianzhou, then left office upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and made prefect of Qianzhou, then left office upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 儂智高反邕州，乘勝掠九郡，以兵圍廣州。

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao rebelled at Yongzhou, seized the victory to plunder nine prefectures, and besieged Guangzhou with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Nong Zhigao rebelled at Yongzhou, seized the victory to plunder nine prefectures, and besieged Guangzhou with troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方顧南事，就喪次起靖為秘書監、知潭州，改桂州，詔以廣南西路委靖經制。

translations.literal: The court was then concerned with southern affairs; from his mourning residence Jing was summoned as Director of the Secretariat and prefect of Tanzhou, changed to Guizhou; an edict entrusted the Guangnan West Circuit to Jing for overall management.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then concerned with southern affairs; from his mourning residence Yu Jing was summoned as director of the Secretariat and prefect of Tanzhou, changed to Guizhou; an edict entrusted the Guangnan West Circuit to Jing for overall management.

sentences.zh: 智高西走邕州，靖策其必結援交阯，而脅諸峒以自固，乃約李德政會兵擊賊於邕州，備萬人糧以待之；

translations.literal: Zhigao fled west to Yongzhou; Jing calculated that he would surely seek aid from Jiaozhi and coerce the various dong to strengthen himself; he therefore arranged with Li Dezheng to join forces and strike the bandits at Yongzhou, preparing provisions for ten thousand men to await them;
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao fled west to Yongzhou; Yu Jing calculated that he would surely seek aid from Jiaozhi and coerce the various dong to strengthen himself; he therefore arranged with Li Dezheng to join forces and strike the bandits at Yongzhou, preparing provisions for ten thousand men to await them;

sentences.zh: 而詔亦給緡錢二萬助德政興師，且約賊平更賞以緡錢二萬。

translations.literal: an edict also granted twenty thousand strings of cash to assist Dezheng in raising troops, with the further promise that when the bandits were pacified another twenty thousand strings would be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: an edict also granted twenty thousand strings of cash to assist Dezheng in raising troops, with the further promise that when the bandits were pacified another twenty thousand strings would be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 又募儂、黃諸姓酋長，皆縻以職，使不與智高合。

translations.literal: He also recruited chieftains of the Nong, Huang, and other surnames, all tethering them with offices so they would not join Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited chieftains of the Nong, Huang, and other surnames, all tethering them with offices so they would not join Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 既而朝廷遣狄青、孫沔將兵共討賊。

translations.literal: Before long the court dispatched Di Qing and Sun Kan to lead troops jointly to suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court dispatched Di Qing and Sun Kan to lead troops jointly to suppress the bandits.

sentences.zh: 青卻交阯，援兵不用，賊平。

translations.literal: Qing turned back Jiaozhi; reinforcements were not used, and the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qing turned back Jiaozhi; reinforcements were not used, and the bandits were pacified.

sentences.zh: 就遷靖給事中。

translations.literal: Jing was thereupon promoted to Supervising Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing was thereupon promoted to supervising attendant.

sentences.zh: 御史梁蒨言賞薄，又遷尚書工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Censor Liang Qian said the reward was too meager, and Jing was further promoted to Vice Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liang Qian said the reward was too meager, and Yu Jing was further promoted to vice minister of public works.

sentences.zh: 初，青兵未至前，戒部將勿戰。

translations.literal: Initially, before Qing's troops arrived, he had warned subordinate generals not to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, before Qing's troops arrived, he had warned subordinate generals not to fight.

sentences.zh: 靖迫鈐轄陳曙出鬥，敗走。

translations.literal: Jing pressured Military Coordinator Chen Shu to sally forth and fight, and they were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing pressured military coordinator Chen Shu to sally forth and fight, and they were defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 青至，按軍法斬曙及指使袁用等於坐，靖瞿然起拜。

translations.literal: When Qing arrived, he executed Shu and Commanders Yuan Yong and others on the spot according to military law; Jing started up and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing arrived, he executed Shu and commanders Yuan Yong and others on the spot according to military law; Yu Jing started up and bowed.

sentences.zh: 及諸將班師，獨留靖廣西，遣人入特磨道擒智高母子弟三人，生致之闕下。

translations.literal: When the generals returned in triumph, Jing alone remained in Guangxi; he sent men into the Temó Trail to capture Zhigao's mother, younger brother, and three sons, delivering them alive to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals returned in triumph, Yu Jing alone remained in Guangxi; he sent men into the Temó Trail to capture Zhigao's mother, younger brother, and three sons, delivering them alive to the capital.

sentences.zh: 加集賢院學士，徙知潭州，又徙青州。

translations.literal: He was added as Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, transferred to prefect of Tanzhou, and again to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was added as academician of the Academy of Worthies, transferred to prefect of Tanzhou, and again to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 交阯蠻申紹泰寇邕州，殺五巡檢。

translations.literal: The Jiaozhi barbarian Shen Shaotai raided Yongzhou and killed five patrol inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaozhi barbarian Shen Shaotai raided Yongzhou and killed five patrol inspectors.

sentences.zh: 以靖安撫廣西，至則召交阯用事臣費嘉祐詰問之，嘉祐至，紿以近邊種落相侵報，誤犯官軍，願悉推治，還所掠及械罪人以自贖。

translations.literal: Jing was made Pacification Commissioner of Guangxi; upon arrival he summoned Jiaozhi's powerful minister Fei Jiayou for questioning; when Jiayou came, he deceived them saying nearby border tribes had mutually raided and reported, mistakenly striking official troops, and wished to have all responsible parties punished, returning captives and criminals to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing was made pacification commissioner of Guangxi; upon arrival he summoned Jiaozhi's powerful minister Fei Jiayou for questioning; when Jiayou came, he deceived them saying nearby border tribes had mutually raided and reported, mistakenly striking official troops, and wished to have all responsible parties punished, returning captives and criminals to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 靖信之，厚謝遣去，嘉祐遂歸，不復出。

translations.literal: Jing believed him, thanked him warmly and sent him away; Jiayou then returned and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing believed him, thanked him warmly and sent him away; Jiayou then returned and did not come out again.

sentences.zh: 知廣州，官至工部尚書，代歸，卒。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Guangzhou, rose to Minister of Public Works, returned upon replacement, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Guangzhou, rose to minister of public works, returned upon replacement, and died.

sentences.zh: 三司使蔡襄為靖言，特贈刑部尚書，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Three Departments Cai Xiang spoke on Jing's behalf, and he was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Justice with the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of the Three Departments Cai Xiang spoke on Yu Jing's behalf, and he was specially posthumously enfeoffed as minister of justice with the posthumous epithet Xiang.

sentences.zh: 靖嘗夢神人告以所終官而死秦亭，故靖常畏西行。

translations.literal: Jing once dreamed that a spirit told him he would die at the rank he ultimately held, at Qin Pavilion; therefore Jing always feared going west.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing once dreamed that a spirit told him he would die at the rank he ultimately held, at Qin Pavilion; therefore he always feared going west.

sentences.zh: 及卒，則江寧府秦淮亭也。

translations.literal: When he died, it was at the Qinhuai Pavilion in Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, it was at the Qinhuai Pavilion in Jiangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彭思永

translations.literal: Peng Siyong
translations.idiomatic: Peng Siyong

sentences.zh: 彭思永，字季長，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Peng Siyong, styled Jichang, was a native of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Siyong, courtesy name Jichang, was a native of Luling.

sentences.zh: 第進士，知南海、分寧縣，通判睦州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Nanhai and Fenning counties and as vice-prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Nanhai and Fenning counties and as vice-prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 台州大水敗城，人多溺，往攝治焉。

translations.literal: Great floods in Taizhou destroyed the city walls and many people drowned; he went to take charge of relief there.
translations.idiomatic: Great floods in Taizhou destroyed the city walls and many people drowned; he went to take charge of relief there.

sentences.zh: 盡葬死者，作文祭之；

translations.literal: He buried all the dead and composed a text to sacrifice to them;
translations.idiomatic: He buried all the dead and composed a text to sacrifice to them;

sentences.zh: 民貧不能葺居，為伐木以助之，數月，公私之舍皆具，城築高於前，而堅亦如之。

translations.literal: the people were too poor to rebuild their dwellings, so he felled timber to assist them; within several months, public and private dwellings were all restored, and the walls were built higher than before and equally solid.
translations.idiomatic: the people were too poor to rebuild their dwellings, so he felled timber to assist them; within several months, public and private dwellings were all restored, and the walls were built higher than before and equally solid.

sentences.zh: 知潮州、常州。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Chaozhou and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Chaozhou and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為侍御史，論內降授官賞之弊，謂斜封非盛世所當有，仁宗深然之。

translations.literal: He entered court as Attending Censor, discussing the abuses of inner-palace bestowal of ranks and rewards, saying that irregular appointments were not what a flourishing age should have; Emperor Renzong deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as attending censor, discussing the abuses of inner-palace bestowal of ranks and rewards, saying that irregular appointments were not what a flourishing age should have; Emperor Renzong deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 皇祐祀明堂前一日，有傳百官皆進秩者。

translations.literal: On the day before the Huangyou Bright Hall sacrifice, word spread that all officials would be advanced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before the Huangyou Bright Hall sacrifice, word spread that all officials would be advanced in rank.

sentences.zh: 思永言不宜濫恩，以益僥幸。

translations.literal: Siyong said indiscriminate grace should not be granted, as it would only increase opportunism.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong said indiscriminate grace should not be granted, as it would only increase opportunism.

sentences.zh: 時張堯佐已貴而猶覬執政，王守忠已受寵而求旄節。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Yaozuo was already honored yet still coveted a place in the government, and Wang Shouzhong had already received favor yet sought a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Yaozuo was already honored yet still coveted a place in the government, and Wang Shouzhong had already received favor yet sought a military commission.

sentences.zh: 思永率同列言之，或曰：「俟命出，未晚也。」

translations.literal: Siyong led his colleagues in speaking on this; some said: "Wait until the edict is issued—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong led his colleagues in speaking on this; some said: "Wait until the edict is issued—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 思永曰：「先事而言，第得罪爾；

translations.literal: Siyong said: "To speak before the fact is merely to risk offense;
translations.idiomatic: Siyong said: "To speak before the fact is merely to risk offense;

sentences.zh: 命一出，不可止矣。」

translations.literal: once the edict is issued, it cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: once the edict is issued, it cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 遂獨抗疏曰：「陛下覃此謬恩，豈為天下孤寒哉。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial alone saying: "Your Majesty grants this mistaken grace—is it for the poor and isolated of all under heaven?
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon submitted a memorial alone saying: "Your Majesty grants this mistaken grace—is it for the poor and isolated of all under heaven?

sentences.zh: 不過為堯佐、守忠取悅眾人耳。

translations.literal: It is nothing but to please the crowd for Yaozuo and Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: It is nothing but to please the crowd for Yaozuo and Shouzhong.

sentences.zh: 外戚秉政，宦侍用權，非社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: Imperial affines holding power and eunuch attendants wielding authority are no blessing to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial affines holding power and eunuch attendants wielding authority are no blessing to the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，中丞郭勸、諫官吳奎為之請，乃以泛恩轉司封員外郎而解臺職，為湖北轉運使。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry; Vice Censor-in-Chief Guo Quan and Remonstrator Wu Kui pleaded on his behalf; he was thereupon transferred to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Rites through general grace and relieved of censorial duty, becoming Transport Commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry; vice censor-in-chief Guo Quan and remonstrator Wu Kui pleaded on his behalf; he was thereupon transferred to assistant director in the Ministry of Rites through general grace and relieved of censorial duty, becoming transport commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 下溪蠻彭仕羲作亂，先移書激罵辰州守。

translations.literal: The Xixi barbarian Peng Shiyi rebelled; he first sent a letter with fierce abuse to the prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Xixi barbarian Peng Shiyi rebelled; he first sent a letter with fierce abuse to the prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 守將討之，思永按部適至，仕羲懼，遣使迎謝，寢其謀。

translations.literal: The defending general attacked him; Siyong happened to be on inspection tour and arrived; Shiyi grew afraid, sent envoys to welcome and apologize, and abandoned his plot.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general attacked him; Siyong happened to be on inspection tour and arrived; Shiyi grew afraid, sent envoys to welcome and apologize, and abandoned his plot.

sentences.zh: 加直史館，為益州路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was added to appointment in the Direct Historiography Office and made Transport Commissioner of Yizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was added to appointment in the Direct Historiography Office and made transport commissioner of Yizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 成都府吏盜公錢，付獄已三歲，出入自如。

translations.literal: A clerk of Chengdu Prefecture stole public funds; after being put in prison for three years, he came and went as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk of Chengdu Prefecture stole public funds; after being put in prison for three years, he came and went as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 思永攝府事甫一日，即具獄。

translations.literal: Siyong took charge of the prefecture for only one day and immediately completed the case.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong took charge of the prefecture for only one day and immediately completed the case.

sentences.zh: 民以楮券為市，藏衣帶中，盜置刃於爪，捷取之，鮮敗者。

translations.literal: The people used paper notes as currency, keeping them in their belts; thieves placed blades in their fingernails and swiftly snatched them—few were caught.
translations.idiomatic: The people used paper notes as currency, keeping them in their belts; thieves placed blades in their fingernails and swiftly snatched them—few were caught.

sentences.zh: 思永得一人詰之，悉黥其黨隸兵間。

translations.literal: Siyong caught one man and interrogated him, then tattooed the entire gang and assigned them among the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong caught one man and interrogated him, then tattooed the entire gang and assigned them among the troops.

sentences.zh: 中使歲祠峨眉，率留成都掊珍玩，價直數百萬錢，悉出於民。

translations.literal: Imperial envoys annually sacrificed at Mount Emei and always stayed in Chengdu to extort precious curios worth millions, all extracted from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys annually sacrificed at Mount Emei and always stayed in Chengdu to extort precious curios worth millions, all extracted from the people.

sentences.zh: 思永朘其三之一，使怒去，而不能有所中傷也。

translations.literal: Siyong reduced this by one third; the envoy left in anger but could do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong reduced this by one third; the envoy left in anger but could do no harm.

sentences.zh: 尋為戶部副使，擢天章閣待制、河北都轉運使、知瀛州。

translations.literal: Soon after he became Vice Commissioner of Revenue, was promoted to Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, Metropolitan Transport Commissioner of Hebei, and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became vice commissioner of revenue, was promoted to awaiting draftsman of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations, metropolitan transport commissioner of Hebei, and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 北俗以桑麻為產籍，民懼賦不敢藝，日益貧，思永始奏更之。

translations.literal: Northern custom used mulberry and hemp as production registers; the people feared taxation and dared not cultivate, growing poorer day by day; Siyong was the first to memorialize for a change.
translations.idiomatic: Northern custom used mulberry and hemp as production registers; the people feared taxation and dared not cultivate, growing poorer day by day; Siyong was the first to memorialize for a change.

sentences.zh: 徒知江寧府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治平中，召為御史中丞。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era he was summoned as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era he was summoned as vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 濮王有稱親之議，言事者爭之，皆斥去。

translations.literal: There was debate over calling the Prince of Pu a parent; remonstrators argued fiercely and were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: There was debate over calling the Prince of Pu a parent; remonstrators argued fiercely and were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 思永更上疏極論曰：「濮王生陛下，而仁宗以陛下為嗣，是仁宗為皇考，而濮王於屬為伯，此天地大義，生人大倫。

translations.literal: Siyong submitted another memorial arguing forcefully: "The Prince of Pu begat Your Majesty, yet Emperor Renzong took Your Majesty as heir—thus Emperor Renzong is imperial father, and the Prince of Pu in kinship terms is paternal uncle; this is the great righteousness of Heaven and Earth and the great norm of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong submitted another memorial arguing forcefully: "The Prince of Pu begat Your Majesty, yet Emperor Renzong took Your Majesty as heir—thus Emperor Renzong is imperial father, and the Prince of Pu in kinship terms is paternal uncle; this is the great righteousness of Heaven and Earth and the great norm of human relations.

sentences.zh: 如乾坤定位，不可得而變也。

translations.literal: It is like the positioning of Heaven and Earth—it cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: It is like the positioning of Heaven and Earth—it cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 陛下為仁廟子，曰考曰親，乃仁廟也；

translations.literal: Your Majesty is the son of Emperor Ren; you call him Father and Parent—that refers to Emperor Ren;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is the son of Emperor Ren; you call him Father and Parent—that refers to Emperor Ren;

sentences.zh: 若更施於濮王，是有二親矣。

translations.literal: if this is also applied to the Prince of Pu, there would be two parents.
translations.idiomatic: if this is also applied to the Prince of Pu, there would be two parents.

sentences.zh: 使王與諸父夷等，無有殊別，則於大孝之心亦為難安。

translations.literal: If the Prince is made equal to other paternal uncles without special distinction, then the heart of great filial piety would also find this hard to accept.
translations.idiomatic: If the Prince is made equal to other paternal uncles without special distinction, then the heart of great filial piety would also find this hard to accept.

sentences.zh: 臣以為當尊為濮國大王，祭告之辭，則曰『侄嗣皇帝書名昭告於皇伯父』。

translations.literal: I believe he should be honored as Prince of Pu, and in the sacrificial announcement it should read: "Nephew and Successor Emperor [name] announces to Imperial Paternal Uncle."
translations.idiomatic: I believe he should be honored as Prince of Pu, and in the sacrificial announcement it should read: "Nephew and Successor Emperor [name] announces to Imperial Paternal Uncle."

sentences.zh: 在王則極尊崇之道，而於仁廟亦無所嫌矣，此萬世之法也。」

translations.literal: For the Prince this is the utmost path of honor, and for Emperor Ren there is also no cause for offense—this is the law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: For the Prince this is the utmost path of honor, and for Emperor Ren there is also no cause for offense—this is the law for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 疏入，英宗感其切至，垂欲施行，而中書持之甚力，卒不果。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Yingzong was moved by its earnestness and was about to implement it, but the Secretariat held fast and in the end it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Yingzong was moved by its earnestness and was about to implement it, but the Secretariat held fast and in the end it did not come to pass.

sentences.zh: 思永仁厚廉恕。

translations.literal: Siyong was benevolent, generous, honest, and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong was benevolent, generous, honest, and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 為兒時，旦起就學，得金釵於門外，默坐其處。

translations.literal: As a child, rising early to go to study, he found a gold hairpin outside the gate and sat silently in that spot.
translations.idiomatic: As a child, rising early to go to study, he found a gold hairpin outside the gate and sat silently in that spot.

sentences.zh: 須臾亡釵者來物色，審之良是，即付之。

translations.literal: Before long the owner of the lost pin came searching; after verifying it was indeed hers, he gave it to her.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the owner of the lost pin came searching; after verifying it was indeed hers, he gave it to her.

sentences.zh: 其人欲謝以錢，思永笑曰：「使我欲之，則匿金矣。」

translations.literal: The person wished to thank him with money; Siyong smiled and said: "If I had wanted it, I would have hidden the gold.
translations.idiomatic: The person wished to thank him with money; Siyong smiled and said: "If I had wanted it, I would have hidden the gold.

sentences.zh: 始就舉，持數釧為資。

translations.literal: When he first went to take the examination, he carried several bracelets as capital.
translations.idiomatic: When he first went to take the examination, he carried several bracelets as capital.

sentences.zh: 同舉者過之，出而玩，或墜其一於袖間，眾相為求索。

translations.literal: Fellow examinees visited; one took them out to play with, and one fell into his sleeve; all searched together.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow examinees visited; one took them out to play with, and one fell into his sleeve; all searched together.

sentences.zh: 思永曰：「數止此耳。」

translations.literal: Siyong said: "The number stops here.
translations.idiomatic: Siyong said: "The number stops here.

sentences.zh: 客去，舉手揖，釧墜於地，眾皆服其量。

translations.literal: When the guest left, he raised his hand in farewell and the bracelet fell to the ground; all admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: When the guest left, he raised his hand in farewell and the bracelet fell to the ground; all admired his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，窶甚，鄉人饋之，無所受。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother he was extremely impoverished; neighbors offered gifts but he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning for his mother he was extremely impoverished; neighbors offered gifts but he accepted none.

sentences.zh: 子：衛，亦孝謹，以父老，棄官家居十餘年，族里稱之。

translations.literal: Son: Wei, also filial and careful; because his father was elderly, he abandoned office and lived at home for more than ten years; kinsmen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Wei, also filial and careful; because his father was elderly, he abandoned office and lived at home for more than ten years; kinsmen praised him.

sentences.zh: 張存，字誠之，冀州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Cun, styled Chengzhi, was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cun, courtesy name Chengzhi, was a native of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為安肅軍判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial aide of Ansu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial aide of Ansu Army.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，詔銓司以身言書判取士，才得二人，存預其選。

translations.literal: In the Tianxi era, an edict ordered the Personnel Bureau to select officials by personal conduct, speech, and document judgment; only two men qualified, and Cun was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxi era, an edict ordered the Personnel Bureau to select officials by personal conduct, speech, and document judgment; only two men qualified, and Cun was among them.

sentences.zh: 改著作佐郎，知大名府朝城縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to Assistant Compiler and served as magistrate of Chaocheng County in Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to assistant compiler and served as magistrate of Chaocheng County in Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寇準為守，異待之。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun was prefect and treated him with special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was prefect and treated him with special regard.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王曙，屢薦為殿中侍御史，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Shu repeatedly recommended him as Attending Censor in the Palace and promoted him to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Wang Shu repeatedly recommended him as attending censor in the palace and promoted him to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初親政，罷百官轉對，存請復之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong first personally assumed governance, the rotation of officials for direct audience was abolished; Cun requested its restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong first personally assumed governance, the rotation of officials for direct audience was abolished; Zhang Cun requested its restoration.

sentences.zh: 又言：「前者曹修古輩同忤旨廢黜，布衣林獻可因上封事竄惡地，恐自今忠直之言，與夫理亂安危之機，蔽而不達。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Previously Cao Xiugu and his like were all dismissed for opposing the imperial will; commoner Lin Xiank submitted a sealed memorial and was banished to a harsh place—I fear that from now on loyal and upright words, and the turning points of order and chaos, safety and danger, will be blocked and not reach you.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Previously Cao Xiugu and his like were all dismissed for opposing the imperial will; commoner Lin Xiank submitted a sealed memorial and was banished to a harsh place—I fear that from now on loyal and upright words, and the turning points of order and chaos, safety and danger, will be blocked and not reach you.

sentences.zh: 因歷引周昌、朱雲、辛慶忌、辛毗事，以開帝意。

translations.literal: He thereupon cited in succession the cases of Zhou Chang, Zhu Yun, Xin Qingji, and Xin Pi to open the Emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon cited in succession the cases of Zhou Chang, Zhu Yun, Xin Qingji, and Xin Pi to open the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 歷京東陝西、河北、轉運使、戶部度支副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Transport Commissioner of Jingdong, Shaanxi, and Hebei, and as Vice Commissioner of Revenue in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as transport commissioner of Jingdong, Shaanxi, and Hebei, and as vice commissioner of revenue.

sentences.zh: 西邊動兵，以天章閣待制為陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: When war was launched on the western frontier, he was made Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and Metropolitan Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When war was launched on the western frontier, he was made awaiting draftsman of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and metropolitan transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 黃德和之誣劉平也，存奏言：「平與敵接戰，自旦至暮，殺傷相當，因德和引卻，以致潰敗。

translations.literal: When Huang Dehe falsely accused Liu Ping, Cun submitted a memorial saying: "Ping engaged the enemy from dawn to dusk with roughly equal casualties; because Dehe withdrew, defeat and rout followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Dehe falsely accused Liu Ping, Zhang Cun submitted a memorial saying: "Ping engaged the enemy from dawn to dusk with roughly equal casualties; because Dehe withdrew, defeat and rout followed.

sentences.zh: 方賊勢甚張，非平搏戰，其勢必不沮；

translations.literal: Just as the bandits' momentum was at its height, had Ping not fought them, their momentum would surely not have been checked;
translations.idiomatic: Just as the bandits' momentum was at its height, had Ping not fought them, their momentum would surely not have been checked;

sentences.zh: 延州孤壘，非平解圍，其城必不守。

translations.literal: Yanzhou was an isolated fortress; had Ping not broken the siege, the city would surely not have been held.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was an isolated fortress; had Ping not broken the siege, the city would surely not have been held.

sentences.zh: 身既陷沒，而不幸又為讒狡所困，邊臣自此無復死節矣。」

translations.literal: He has already fallen in battle, yet unhappily is further trapped by slanderous and cunning men—from this border officials will no longer die for their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He has already fallen in battle, yet unhappily is further trapped by slanderous and cunning men—from this border officials will no longer die for their integrity.

sentences.zh: 朝廷采其說，始遣文彥博按治，由是平得直，而德和誅。

translations.literal: The court adopted his proposal and first dispatched Wen Yanbo to investigate; thereby Ping was vindicated and Dehe was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposal and first dispatched Wen Yanbo to investigate; thereby Liu Ping was vindicated and Dehe was executed.

sentences.zh: 元昊求款附，議者猶執攻討之策。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao sought to submit and attach himself, yet debaters still clung to strategies of attack and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao sought to submit, yet debaters still clung to strategies of attack and suppression.

sentences.zh: 存建言：「兵役不息，生民疲弊。

translations.literal: Cun submitted a proposal: "Military service does not cease and the people are worn and impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cun submitted a proposal: "Military service does not cease and the people are worn and impoverished.

sentences.zh: 敵既有悛心，雖名號未正，頗羈縻之。」

translations.literal: The enemy already has a mind to reform; though his titles are not yet regularized, he should be somewhat tethered and managed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy already has a mind to reform; though his titles are not yet regularized, he should be tethered and managed.

sentences.zh: 遷龍圖閣直學士，知延州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician Directly Attached to the Hall of Dragon Designs and made prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Dragon Designs Pavilion and made prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以母老憚行，徙澤州，還為待制。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he feared the journey and was transferred to Zezhou, then returned as awaiting draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was old he feared the journey and was transferred to Zezhou, then returned as awaiting draftsman.

sentences.zh: 逾年，知成德軍，復學士。

translations.literal: After a year he served as prefect of Chengdé Army and was restored as academician.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he served as prefect of Chengdé Army and was restored as academician.

sentences.zh: 契丹與元昊結昏，陰謀相首尾，聚兵塞上而求關南。

translations.literal: The Khitan formed a marriage alliance with Yuan Hao and secretly plotted to act in concert, massing troops on the border to demand the southern passes.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan formed a marriage alliance with Yuan Hao and secretly plotted to act in concert, massing troops on the border to demand the southern passes.

sentences.zh: 存言：「河北城久不治，宜留意。」

translations.literal: Cun said: "The cities of Hebei have long gone unrepaired; attention should be paid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cun said: "The cities of Hebei have long gone unrepaired; attention should be paid."

sentences.zh: 乃以為都運使，盡城諸州。

translations.literal: He was thereupon made Metropolitan Transport Commissioner and walled all the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon made metropolitan transport commissioner and walled all the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 入知開封府，復使河北。

translations.literal: He entered court as prefect of Kaifeng and was again dispatched to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as prefect of Kaifeng and was again dispatched to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 王則反，坐失察，降知汀州。

translations.literal: When Wang Ze rebelled, Cun was punished for failure of oversight and demoted to prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ze rebelled, Zhang Cun was punished for failure of oversight and demoted to prefect of Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 存婿李敭之弟李教，因醉為妖言，事覺自縊死。

translations.literal: Cun's son-in-law Li Yang's younger brother Li Jiao, while drunk, uttered sorcerous words; when the matter was discovered he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cun's son-in-law Li Yang's younger brother Li Jiao, while drunk, uttered sorcerous words; when the matter was discovered he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 或言教不死，在貝州，父母私屬以存故得免。

translations.literal: Some said Jiao did not die but was in Beizhou; his parents and private associates were spared on Cun's account.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Jiao did not die but was in Beizhou; his parents and private associates were spared on Zhang Cun's account.

sentences.zh: 御史案驗無狀，猶奪職知池州，又徙郴。

translations.literal: Censors investigated and found no substance, yet Cun was still stripped of office and made prefect of Chizhou, then transferred to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Censors investigated and found no substance, yet Zhang Cun was still stripped of office and posted as prefect of Chizhou, then transferred to Chen.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃復職，以吏部侍郎致仕，凡十五年，積遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time his office was restored; he retired as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; over fifteen years he accumulated promotions to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time his office was restored; he retired as vice minister of personnel; over fifteen years he accumulated promotions to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 存性孝友，嘗為蜀郡，得奇繒文錦以歸，悉布之堂上，恣兄弟擇取。

translations.literal: Cun was filial and friendly by nature; once while serving in a Shu prefecture he obtained rare silks and brocades and brought them home, spreading them all in the hall and letting his brothers choose freely.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cun was filial and friendly by nature; once while serving in a Shu prefecture he obtained rare silks and brocades and brought them home, spreading them all in the hall and letting his brothers choose freely.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「兄弟，手足也；

translations.literal: He often said: "Brothers are hands and feet;
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "Brothers are hands and feet;

sentences.zh: 妻妾，外舍人耳。

translations.literal: wives and concubines are merely outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: wives and concubines are merely outsiders.

sentences.zh: 奈何先外人而後手足乎？」

translations.literal: How can one put outsiders before hands and feet?
translations.idiomatic: How can one put outsiders before hands and feet?

sentences.zh: 收恤宗屬，嫁聘窮嫠，不使一人失所。

translations.literal: He gathered and supported clansmen, arranging marriages and betrothals for impoverished widows, not letting a single person lose their place.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered and supported clansmen, arranging marriages and betrothals for impoverished widows, not letting a single person lose their place.

sentences.zh: 家居矜莊，子孫非正衣冠不見。

translations.literal: At home he was dignified and solemn; he would not see his children and grandchildren unless they wore proper dress.
translations.idiomatic: At home he was dignified and solemn; he would not see his children and grandchildren unless they wore proper dress.

sentences.zh: 與賓友燕接，垂足危坐終日，未嘗傾倚。

translations.literal: When feasting and receiving guests and friends, he sat upright with feet hanging all day long, never leaning back.
translations.idiomatic: When feasting and receiving guests and friends, he sat upright with feet hanging all day long, never leaning back.

sentences.zh: 棗強河決，勢逼冀城，或勸使他徒，曰：「吾家，眾所望也，苟輕舉動，使一州吏民何以自安。」

translations.literal: When the Zaoqiang River burst its banks and the flood threatened Jicheng, some urged him to move elsewhere; he said: "My household is what the multitude looks to; if I act rashly, how can the officials and people of the whole prefecture find peace?
translations.idiomatic: When the Zaoqiang River burst its banks and the flood threatened Jicheng, some urged him to move elsewhere; he said: "My household is what the multitude looks to; if I act rashly, how can the officials and people of the whole prefecture find peace?"

sentences.zh: 訖不徙。

translations.literal: In the end he did not move.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not move.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十八，諡恭安。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-eight; his posthumous title was Gong'an (Respectful and Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-eight and was granted the posthumous epithet Respectful and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 論曰：蔡襄、王素、余靖，皆昭陵賢御史也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Cai Xiang, Wang Su, and Yu Jing were all worthy censors of Emperor Renzong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Cai Xiang, Wang Su, and Yu Jing were all worthy censors of Emperor Renzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 襄數論治體，推韓琦、范仲淹之賢。

translations.literal: Xiang repeatedly discussed the fundamentals of governance and promoted the worth of Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang repeatedly discussed the fundamentals of governance and promoted the worth of Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan.

sentences.zh: 素請罷不急之賞，論仁宗納二女子為非。

translations.literal: Su requested abolition of non-urgent rewards and argued that Emperor Renzong's acceptance of two women was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su requested abolition of non-urgent rewards and argued that Emperor Renzong's acceptance of two women was wrong.

sentences.zh: 靖黜夏竦、王舉正為不可用。

translations.literal: Jing dismissed Xia Song and Wang Juzheng as unfit for use.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing dismissed Xia Song and Wang Juzheng as unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 蓋仁宗銳於求治，數君子提綱振紀而扶持之，卒成慶曆之治，良有以也。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was keen to seek good governance; these several gentlemen raised the standards and restored discipline while supporting him, ultimately achieving the governance of the Qingli era—there was good reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong was keen to seek good governance; these several gentlemen raised the standards and restored discipline while supporting him, ultimately achieving the governance of the Qingli era—there was good reason for it.

sentences.zh: 夫襄精於民事，吏不敢欺；

translations.literal: Xiang was skilled in civil affairs and clerks dared not deceive him;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xiang was skilled in civil affairs and clerks dared not deceive him;

sentences.zh: 靖用兵蠻徼，卒收功名；

translations.literal: Jing used troops on the barbarian frontier and ultimately won merit and fame;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jing used troops on the barbarian frontier and ultimately won merit and fame;

sentences.zh: 素在西邊多惠政，其尹開封，雖頗厭煩劇，再為渭州，邊民老幼，至相率稱賀，其惠之在民者，深矣哉。

translations.literal: Su enacted many benevolent policies on the western frontier; though as prefect of Kaifeng he grew somewhat weary of arduous duties, when he again served as prefect of Weizhou, old and young among the border people even joined in congratulating him—the depth of his bounty to the people was profound indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su enacted many benevolent policies on the western frontier; though as prefect of Kaifeng he grew weary of arduous duties, when he again served as prefect of Weizhou, old and young among the border people joined in congratulating him—the depth of his bounty to the people was profound indeed.

sentences.zh: 若呂溱論陳執中，則不欲以口舌中人。

translations.literal: As for Lü Zhen's discussion of Chen Zhizhong, he did not wish to strike at a man with words alone.
translations.idiomatic: As for Lü Zhen's discussion of Chen Zhizhong, he did not wish to strike at a man with words alone.

sentences.zh: 彭思永名士，能識程頤之賢，而不能容歐陽修之剛；

translations.literal: Peng Siyong was a renowned scholar, able to recognize the worth of Cheng Yi yet unable to tolerate the forthrightness of Ouyang Xiu;
translations.idiomatic: Peng Siyong was a renowned scholar, able to recognize the worth of Cheng Yi yet unable to tolerate the forthrightness of Ouyang Xiu;

sentences.zh: 蔣之奇之誣，竟坐是黜，士論憾之。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhiqi's false accusation ultimately led to his dismissal on that account, and scholarly opinion regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhiqi's false accusation ultimately led to Siyong's dismissal on that account, and scholarly opinion regretted it.

sentences.zh: 劉平之死，眾莫敢言，張存獨處而明之。

translations.literal: At Liu Ping's death, none dared speak; Zhang Cun alone stood apart and clarified the truth.
translations.idiomatic: At Liu Ping's death, none dared speak; Zhang Cun alone stood apart and clarified the truth.

sentences.zh: 使忠義之氣，死而復生，較之諸人，亦無忝焉。

translations.literal: He caused the spirit of loyalty and righteousness to live again after death; compared with the others, he was not unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: He caused the spirit of loyalty and righteousness to live again after death; compared with the others, he was not unworthy.
